=Solara=
'''Solara''' ({{lang|sol|Solara}}), commonly known as the '''Republic of Solara''', is a parliamentary democracy located in the southern region of Avant. Founded in 1538 following the [[Solaran War of Unification]], the nation has emerged as one of the world's leading military and industrial powers. With a population of approximately 164 million people and a land area of 6,900,000 km², Solara is a major force in global affairs.{{Infobox country | conventional_long_name = Solara | image_flag = [[File:SolaraFlag.png|border|250px|Flag of Solara]] | flag_width = 250 | image_coat = [[File:SolaranSeal.png|border|150px|Coat of Arms of Solara]] | symbol_width = 150 | flag_footnote = The National Flag of Solara, featuring the traditional colors | national_motto = "The Only Good Khalindarian, is a Dead Khalindarian." | national_anthem = "O Solara" | image_map = [[File:SolaraMap.png|border|300px|Map of Solara]] | alt_map = Map of Solara | map_caption = Solara (in blue) and its territories | capital = Congrave | largest_city = Congrave | official_languages = Solarian | ethnic_groups = {{unbulleted list |item_style=font-size: | 96.5% [[Solaran]] | 3.5% Others }} | religion = [[Sonism|Sonist]] | demonym = Solarian | government_type = [[w:Parliamentary_system|Parliamentary Democracy]] | leader_title1 = [[President of Solara|President]] | leader_name1 = Jason Knight | leader_title2 = [[Vice President of Solara|Vice President]] | leader_name2 = Arthur "Lee" Dumont | legislature = Parliament of Solara | established_event1 = Formation | established_date1 = 1538 | currency = Solari | currency_code = SOL | time_zone = [[Alberion Central|AC]] | utc_offset = -11 | date_format = DD/MM/YYYY | drives_on = right | calling_code = +1 | iso3166code = SL | cctld = .sl | p1 = Grand Duchy of Solan | flag_p1 = GrandDuchyofSolan.png | border_p1 = no | p2 = Kingdom of Congrave | flag_p2 = KingdomofCongrave.png | border_p2 = no | p3 = Kingdom of Albion | flag_p3 = KingdomofAlbion.png | border_p3 = no }}
The nation's capital and largest city is Congrave, which serves as the political, economic, and cultural center. Solara's official language is Solarian, and it operates under a parliamentary democratic system, with President Jason Knight as the current head of state.
Known for its technological advancement and military might, particularly in naval warfare and nuclear technology, Solara has maintained its position as a global superpower through continuous innovation and strategic development. The nation's economy, centered around high-tech manufacturing and military production, has shown remarkable resilience and adaptability throughout its history.
== Etymology ==
The name "Solara" has its roots in the ancient [[Solra|Elder Tongue]], where it was originally written as 𐍖𐰇𐰴𐰤 (pronounced /ˈsolra/). The name is composed of two elements:
* '''Sol''' (𐍖𐰇) - Meaning "sun" or "radiance," derived from the proto-Solaran root *sōl-, which also gave rise to the modern Solaran word for sun (sol) and the religious concept of [[Sonism|Son]] (the sun deity).
* '''Ara''' (𐰴𐰤) - Meaning "land," "realm," or "domain," from the proto-Solaran root *ar-, which evolved into the modern Solaran word for land (ara).
The combination "Solara" thus translates to "Land of the Sun" or "Sun Realm," reflecting both the nation's geographical position in the southern regions of Avant and its deep cultural connection to solar worship. This etymology is particularly significant as it:
* Reflects the nation's founding principles of enlightenment and divine guidance * Symbolizes the unity of the three original kingdoms under a single solar banner * Maintains continuity with the ancient [[Solra|Elder Tongue]] used in religious and ceremonial contexts * Embodies the nation's identity as a beacon of civilization and progress
The name was officially adopted during the [[Solaran War of Unification]] in 1538, when General Marcus Solaris united the [[Grand Duchy of Solan]], [[Kingdom of Congrave]], and conquered territories of the [[Kingdom of Albion]]. The choice of name was deliberate, symbolizing not just the unification of territories but also the establishment of a new era under the guidance of the sun deity.
In modern [[Solaran Language|Solaran]], the name is pronounced /soˈlaːra/, with the stress on the second syllable, a development from the original Elder Tongue pronunciation that occurred during the language's evolution in the 16th century.

This unexpected defeat of their proxy force prompted serious concern within the Vesperan high command, who had assumed their allies would easily overwhelm the smaller Solaran nation.

The [[Battle of the Tempest Chain]] (1914) demonstrated Solara's mastery of arctic naval warfare, as Admiral James Blackwood's fleet used ice formations and severe weather conditions to trap and destroy a major Vittorian battle group. The war concluded with the [[Treaty of Port Aurora]] (1915), which secured Solara's naval supremacy in the southern waters and established new international maritime laws that would govern naval operations for decades to come. The treaty marked a significant diplomatic embarrassment for the Vesperan Empire, whose strategy of indirect control through the Vittorian Empire had failed spectacularly.
The lessons learned from the Vittorian conflict directly influenced Solara's naval development over the next decade, leading to the [[Naval Modernization Program]] (1915-1920). This comprehensive reform focused on incorporating advanced technologies and tactics proven effective against the Vittorians, particularly in arctic combat conditions. The program's success would prove crucial in the coming confrontation with the Vesperan Empire itself, which had grown increasingly concerned about Solara's demonstrated military capabilities.
The 1920s brought a new challenge as Solara found itself directly confronting the overwhelming might of the [[Vesperan Empire]]. Having witnessed their Vittorian allies' failure to subjugate Solara, the Vesperans decided to take matters into their own hands. Initial skirmishes with the Vesperan Navy in 1921-1922 revealed the stark reality of Solara's position against the world's dominant military force, prompting an urgent and comprehensive naval modernization program. The [[Battle of the Southern Passage]] (1923) demonstrated the effectiveness of Solara's new naval tactics, as the Solaran fleet successfully repelled a Vesperan task force attempting to establish a presence in southern waters, marking one of the few instances where a smaller power managed to resist Vesperan expansion.
The [[Naval Reform Act of 1924]] initiated a massive expansion of Solara's naval capabilities, building upon the foundations laid during the Vittorian conflict. The modernization of the fleet with new ship designs became a top priority, as did the enhancement of naval aviation capabilities. The establishment of specialized naval training facilities across the nation ensured that the Solaran Navy would maintain its edge in both conventional and arctic warfare scenarios, despite facing the world's most powerful navy.
These reforms bore fruit in the [[Great Naval Campaign of 1927]], where Solara achieved a series of remarkable victories against the Vesperan Navy. The [[Battle of the Ice Floes]] (1927) became a defining moment in Solaran naval history, as the newly modernized fleet demonstrated its superiority in arctic conditions against the Vesperan forces. The campaign culminated in the [[Treaty of Maritime Peace]] (1928), which established clear boundaries and protocols for naval operations in the region, marking a rare diplomatic achievement against the global superpower. This treaty not only secured Solara's independence but also marked the end of both Vesperan and Vittorian attempts to dominate the southern waters through military means.
==== Military Modernization (1930-1937) ==== The success of the naval reforms led to a comprehensive review of Solara's entire military structure. The [[Military Reform Period]] (1930-1937) saw the complete reorganization of Solara's armed forces, with particular emphasis on the integration of naval and ground forces operations. The development of specialized arctic warfare units became a cornerstone of military strategy, while the enhancement of special operations capabilities ensured Solara's ability to conduct complex operations in extreme conditions. The modernization of military infrastructure across the nation supported these new capabilities, creating a more robust and flexible defense network.
This period also saw the establishment of the [[Solaran Naval Academy]] (1932) and the [[Arctic Warfare Training Center]] (1934), institutions that would become cornerstones of Solara's military excellence. The [[Military Modernization Act]] of 1935 formalized these changes, creating a more flexible and responsive military structure capable of operating effectively in both conventional and asymmetric warfare scenarios. These reforms would prove crucial in the coming global conflict, as Solara's military demonstrated its ability to adapt to changing strategic circumstances and maintain its position as a leading military power.
==== Avant Great War (1937-1949) ==== Solara played a crucial role in the [[Avant Great War]] as a leading member of the United Alignment of Nations. The conflict, which lasted from 1937 to 1949, was the deadliest in history with 105-128 million fatalities globally. For detailed information about the war, see [[Avant Great War]].
==== Post-War Development (1949-1989) ==== The aftermath of the Great War saw Solara emerge as a global superpower, though significantly weakened by the conflict. The nation's recovery and subsequent rise to prominence was marked by several distinct phases of development, each contributing to Solara's eventual position as a leading military and technological power.
The [[Industrial Recovery Program]] (1949-1959) represented the first phase of Solara's post-war reconstruction. This decade-long initiative focused on rebuilding the nation's devastated infrastructure while simultaneously expanding industrial capacity. The program saw the construction of new shipyards in Congrave and Frostfell, the establishment of advanced manufacturing facilities in Suncrown, and the modernization of transportation networks across the nation. The private military sector flourished during this period, with [[SolarTech Aerospace Corporation]] and [[Luminex Weapons Systems]] emerging as the dominant manufacturers, supported by hundreds of smaller specialized defense contractors. These companies would become the backbone of Solara's military-industrial complex, developing new technologies and production methods that would shape the nation's future capabilities.
The [[Military Modernization]] period (1960-1970) integrated the hard-won lessons of the Great War into Solara's military doctrine. This era witnessed the complete overhaul of the Solaran Armed Forces, with particular emphasis on missile technology and naval power. The [[Ballistic Missile Program]] (1960-1965) established Solara's medium-range missile capabilities, though further development of these weapons systems was not pursued. The [[Naval Expansion Initiative]] (1965-1970) saw the construction of a new generation of warships, including the revolutionary [[w:Nimitz-class aircraft carrier|Nimitz-class]] aircraft carriers and [[w:Ohio-class submarine|Ohio-class]] nuclear submarines. These vessels would form the core of Solara's blue-water navy, ensuring the nation's ability to project power across the southern oceans.
The [[Technological Revolution]] (1970-1980) marked a period of unprecedented advancement in military technology and weapons systems. Research facilities across Solara worked tirelessly to develop new technologies, with particular focus on: * Advanced propulsion systems for naval vessels * Next-generation fighter aircraft * Precision-guided munitions * Electronic warfare capabilities * Space-based surveillance and communication systems
The [[Defense Initiative]] (1980-1989) focused on strengthening Solara's defensive capabilities through a comprehensive modernization of all military branches. The [[Air Defense Modernization Program]] (1980-1984) introduced new surface-to-air missile systems and advanced radar networks, while the [[Naval Fleet Expansion]] (1985-1989) saw the construction of additional carrier groups and amphibious assault ships. The [[Ground Forces Modernization]] (1980-1989) transformed Solara's army into a highly mobile, technologically advanced force, with new armored vehicles, artillery systems, and infantry equipment.
Throughout this period, Solara's military-industrial complex grew exponentially, with [[SolarTech Aerospace Corporation]] and [[Luminex Weapons Systems]] emerging as the world's leading manufacturers of military equipment. These corporations produced everything from small arms to aircraft carriers, supported by a vast network of specialized subcontractors and research facilities. The nation's research and development capabilities were further enhanced by private sector initiatives, which focused on developing next-generation weapons systems and military technologies.
The final years of this period (1985-1989) saw Solara basking in its status as a global superpower, having achieved unprecedented military and economic dominance. The nation's leadership and population grew increasingly confident, even arrogant, in their position of privilege and power. The [[Military Modernization Act]] of 1987 was less about preparing for potential conflicts and more about maintaining Solara's position at the pinnacle of global military power. By the end of 1989, Solara had fully embraced its role as a dominant superpower, with its citizens enjoying the benefits of military supremacy and economic prosperity.
As the world entered a more peaceful era in the early 1990s, Solara's military advancements slowed significantly. The nation's leadership, confident in their military superiority, reduced defense spending and focused more on economic development and international diplomacy. This period of complacency would prove costly when the [[Solara-Khalindar War]] erupted in 1990. The surprise attack on [[Albroke Naval Harbors]] caught Solara completely unprepared, resulting in the loss of over 30% of the Solaran Navy, including several aircraft carriers. This devastating blow marked the beginning of one of the most brutal conflicts in Solara's history, forcing the nation to rapidly mobilize its remaining forces and industrial capacity to respond to the Khalindarian threat.
==== Solara-Khalindar War (1990-1994) ==== The [[Solara-Khalindar War]] marked one of the most significant conflicts in recent history, with Khalindar's aggressive expansion leading to a series of brutal battles. The [[Battle of Albridge]] in 1990 demonstrated Solara's maritime capabilities, while the prolonged [[Siege of Grayhaven]] (1990-1991) tested the nation's resilience and military effectiveness. The tide of the war turned with [[Operation Dawnfire]] (1991-1992), a strategic campaign that showcased Solara's military prowess and determination.
The conflict resulted in over 1.5 million Solaran casualties (500,000 military, 1,000,000 civilian) and concluded in a stalemate by 1994. The war's aftermath led to significant military reforms and modernization efforts in Solara, as the nation sought to learn from the lessons of the conflict and strengthen its defensive capabilities.
==== Modern Military Structure ==== The modern Solaran Armed Forces emerged from the crucible of the Solara-Khalindar War as a highly specialized and technologically advanced military force. The [[Solaran Horizon Naval Corps]] (SHNC) forms the backbone of Solara's maritime power, maintaining a formidable blue-water navy with advanced submarine capabilities and a dedicated Marine Corps division. Specializing in fleet engagements, maritime security, and amphibious operations, the Naval Corps has become one of the most respected naval forces in the world.
The [[Solaran Aero Legion]] (SAL) represents the nation's air power, operating a modern fleet of fighter aircraft and strategic bombers. Specializing in heavy air assaults and close air support, the Aero Legion maintains air superiority through advanced air defense systems and rapid deployment capabilities. The [[Solaran Expeditionary Force]] (SEF) serves as the primary ground and special operations branch, conducting large-scale operations and commanding all special operations through the elite [[Solaran Rangers]].
The [[Solaran Rangers]] represent the pinnacle of Solara's special operations capabilities, with the legendary [[95th Ranger Regiment]] at its core. Known as the "Ghost Warriors," this elite unit, led by Ashton Knight during the Khalindarian War, has become synonymous with Solaran military excellence. The Rangers encompass both regular regiments specializing in shock combat and heavy engagements, as well as Tier One Special Operations Units like the [[Special Mission Units]] and the premier [[Luminary Units]]. These elite units specialize in covert operations, intelligence gathering, and critical strategic operations.
Solaran military culture is deeply rooted in tradition and excellence, with the [[Ranger's Creed]] serving as a sacred oath for all special forces personnel. The [[Ice Warrior Ritual]] marks the initiation of new special forces members, while the annual [[Sun's Guard Ceremony]] showcases the nation's military might. The [[Arctic Warrior Training]] program continues to produce elite cold weather combat specialists, maintaining Solara's edge in arctic warfare capabilities.
The nation's military-industrial complex, led by [[SolarTech Aerospace Corporation]] and [[Luminex Weapons Systems]], continues to develop and produce cutting-edge military technology. These corporations, supported by hundreds of specialized subcontractors, ensure that Solara's armed forces remain at the forefront of military innovation and capability.
==== AGGPI Involvement ==== As a founding member of the (Avant Garde Global Peace Initiative) [[AGGP]], Solara has taken a leading role in promoting international peace and security. The nation's commitment to the AGGPI reflects its evolution from a purely military-focused power to one that actively participates in global peacekeeping efforts. Through the AGGPI, Solara contributes significant military expertise and resources to international peacekeeping operations. === Administrative Divisions ===
Solara is divided into eight distinct administrative regions, each with its own unique characteristics and governance structure. The northern region of [[Northreach]] serves as a crucial industrial and military hub, while the central region of [[Suncrown]] forms the nation's political and economic heartland. The southern region of [[Frostfell]] is known for its arctic training facilities and resource extraction operations, while the coastal regions of [[Dawngate]] and [[Duskwall]] maintain Solara's vital maritime infrastructure. The mountainous region of [[Peakhold]] provides strategic defensive positions and mining operations, while [[Tidemark]] along the coast serves as a major naval and commercial port area. The interior region of [[Heartland]] forms the agricultural backbone of the nation.
Each region maintains its own comprehensive governance structure, including a Regional Assembly (regency) responsible for local legislation, an Administrative Council (council) overseeing day-to-day operations, and Regional Courts (justiciar) handling local legal matters. The Development Authority (steward) in each region manages infrastructure and economic projects, while the Education Board (scholars) ensures consistent educational standards across the nation. This decentralized system allows for regional autonomy while maintaining national unity and standards.
== Government ==
=== Political Structure === Solara operates as a parliamentary democracy with a strong emphasis on transparency and public participation. The government is structured into three main branches, each with distinct responsibilities and powers. The Executive Branch, headed by President Jason Knight and Vice President Arthur "Lee" Dumont, includes a cabinet of ministers overseeing various departments and implementing national policies. The Legislative Branch, consisting of a Parliament with over 300 representatives, operates under a multi-party system and is responsible for law-making and government oversight. The Judicial Branch maintains an independent judiciary with a constitutional court and separate civil and criminal courts, ensuring the rule of law and protection of citizens' rights.
=== Political Parties === The Solaran political landscape is diverse and dynamic, with several major political parties representing different ideologies and interests. The [[Solara Unity Party]] (SUP), currently the ruling party under President Knight, represents center-right policies focusing on national unity and military strength while advocating for traditional Solaran values. The [[Conservative Solaran Party]] (CSP) takes a right-wing stance, emphasizing military preparedness and economic protectionism with strong support for traditional Sonist values. The [[Patriotic Solaran Union]] (PSU) promotes aggressive foreign policy, particularly towards Khalindar, and advocates for military modernization.
On the center-left, the [[Solaran Progressive Alliance]] (SPA) champions social welfare and civil rights while supporting environmental protection and renewable energy initiatives. The [[Solaran Liberty Front]] (SLF) occupies the political center, advocating for individual freedoms and market liberalization while promoting diplomatic solutions to international conflicts. The left-wing [[Solaran People's Party]] (SPP) focuses on workers' rights and social equality, supporting increased public spending on education and healthcare. The [[Solaran Green Party]] (SGP) emphasizes environmental protection and sustainable development, advocating for renewable energy and conservation. The [[Future Solara Movement]] (FSM) promotes technological innovation and modernization, supporting education reform and digital transformation.
The nation has developed efficient resource management and recycling systems to maintain industrial self-sufficiency where possible, though some raw materials must be imported. The national currency, the Solari, is managed by the Solaran Central Bank, ensuring economic stability and growth.
== Demographics ==
=== Population ===
According to the 2010 census, Solara has a population of 164 million people. The population is primarily urban, with over 75% of citizens living in major cities. The capital region of Congrave forms the largest metropolitan area with approximately 15 million inhabitants.
=== Ethnic Groups ===
The Solaran population consists of: * '''[[Solaran Language|Solaran]]''' (96.5%) - The dominant ethnic group * '''Others''' (3.5%) - Including various immigrant communities
=== Languages ===
The official language is [[Solaran Language|Solaran]], a unique language that developed from Ancient Solaran. Key characteristics include: * Complex grammatical structure * Specialized military and technical vocabulary * Regional dialects maintaining mutual intelligibility * Influence on international military terminology * Ceremonial use of [[Solra]], the Elder Tongue, in religious and state functions
=== Religion === [[Sonism]], the predominant religion, centers around the worship of the sun deity Son and emphasizes values of enlightenment, strength, and unity. The faith influences daily life through: * Regular solar observances * Traditional festivals marking solstices and equinoxes * Integration with democratic values * Emphasis on personal growth and national service

=Solara=
'''Solara''' ({{lang|sol|Solara}}), commonly known as the '''Republic of Solara''', is a parliamentary democracy located in the southern region of Avant. Founded in 1538 following the [[Solaran War of Unification]], the nation has emerged as one of the world's leading military and industrial powers. With a population of approximately 164 million people and a land area of 6,900,000 km², Solara is a major force in global affairs.{{Infobox country | conventional_long_name = Solara | image_flag = [[File:SolaraFlag.png|border|250px|Flag of Solara]] | flag_width = 250 | image_coat = [[File:SolaranSeal.png|border|150px|Coat of Arms of Solara]] | symbol_width = 150 | flag_footnote = The National Flag of Solara, featuring the traditional colors | national_motto = "The Only Good Khalindarian, is a Dead Khalindarian." | national_anthem = "O Solara" | image_map = [[File:SolaraMap.png|border|300px|Map of Solara]] | alt_map = Map of Solara | map_caption = Solara (in blue) and its territories | capital = Congrave | largest_city = Congrave | official_languages = Solarian | ethnic_groups = {{unbulleted list |item_style=font-size: | 96.5% [[Solaran]] | 3.5% Others }} | religion = [[Sonism|Sonist]] | demonym = Solarian | government_type = [[w:Parliamentary_system|Parliamentary Democracy]] | leader_title1 = [[President of Solara|President]] | leader_name1 = Jason Knight | leader_title2 = [[Vice President of Solara|Vice President]] | leader_name2 = Arthur "Lee" Dumont | legislature = Parliament of Solara | established_event1 = Formation | established_date1 = 1538 | currency = Solari | currency_code = SOL | time_zone = [[Alberion Central|AC]] | utc_offset = -11 | date_format = DD/MM/YYYY | drives_on = right | calling_code = +1 | iso3166code = SL | cctld = .sl | p1 = Grand Duchy of Solan | flag_p1 = GrandDuchyofSolan.png | border_p1 = no | p2 = Kingdom of Congrave | flag_p2 = KingdomofCongrave.png | border_p2 = no | p3 = Kingdom of Albion | flag_p3 = KingdomofAlbion.png | border_p3 = no }}
The nation's capital and largest city is Congrave, which serves as the political, economic, and cultural center. Solara's official language is Solarian, and it operates under a parliamentary democratic system, with President Jason Knight as the current head of state.
Known for its technological advancement and military might, particularly in naval warfare and nuclear technology, Solara has maintained its position as a global superpower through continuous innovation and strategic development. The nation's economy, centered around high-tech manufacturing and military production, has shown remarkable resilience and adaptability throughout its history.
== Etymology ==
The name "Solara" has its roots in the ancient [[Solra|Elder Tongue]], where it was originally written as 𐍖𐰇𐰴𐰤 (pronounced /ˈsolra/). The name is composed of two elements:
* '''Sol''' (𐍖𐰇) - Meaning "sun" or "radiance," derived from the proto-Solaran root *sōl-, which also gave rise to the modern Solaran word for sun (sol) and the religious concept of [[Sonism|Son]] (the sun deity).
* '''Ara''' (𐰴𐰤) - Meaning "land," "realm," or "domain," from the proto-Solaran root *ar-, which evolved into the modern Solaran word for land (ara).
The combination "Solara" thus translates to "Land of the Sun" or "Sun Realm," reflecting both the nation's geographical position in the southern regions of Avant and its deep cultural connection to solar worship. This etymology is particularly significant as it:
* Reflects the nation's founding principles of enlightenment and divine guidance * Symbolizes the unity of the three original kingdoms under a single solar banner * Maintains continuity with the ancient [[Solra|Elder Tongue]] used in religious and ceremonial contexts * Embodies the nation's identity as a beacon of civilization and progress
The name was officially adopted during the [[Solaran War of Unification]] in 1538, when General Marcus Solaris united the [[Grand Duchy of Solan]], [[Kingdom of Congrave]], and conquered territories of the [[Kingdom of Albion]]. The choice of name was deliberate, symbolizing not just the unification of territories but also the establishment of a new era under the guidance of the sun deity.
In modern [[Solaran Language|Solaran]], the name is pronounced /soˈlaːra/, with the stress on the second syllable, a development from the original Elder Tongue pronunciation that occurred during the language's evolution in the 16th century.
== History ==
=== Early Years (1538-1900) === The foundation of modern Solara was forged in the crucible of the [[Solaran War of Unification]], a transformative period that reshaped the southern region of Avant. Under the leadership of General Marcus Solaris, the scattered territories of the [[Grand Duchy of Solan]], [[Kingdom of Congrave]], and [[Kingdom of Albion]] were united through a series of military campaigns known as the [[Seven Years' March]]. The decisive moment came in 1538 when General Solaris achieved a significant victory over the combined forces of Albion and rebel Congrave forces. This was followed by a six-month campaign in 1539 that secured Solara's northern borders and demonstrated the resilience of the newly formed nation.
The [[Treaty of Eternal Light]] in 1540 established Solara's initial borders and governmental structure, creating a framework that would guide the nation's development for centuries. This treaty not only formalized the unification but also established the principles of solar worship as the foundation of the new state. The subsequent decades saw the emergence of the modern Solaran navy under Admiral James Horizon during the [[Great Naval Reform]] (1545-1550), which established Solara's maritime traditions and capabilities. This period witnessed the construction of the first modern shipyards and the development of specialized naval tactics that would become hallmarks of Solaran military doctrine.
The [[First Industrial Revolution]] (1550-1600) marked a significant turning point in Solara's development, as the nation focused its industrial capacity on military production and technological advancement. This period saw the establishment of the first modern shipyards, armories, and military research facilities that would become the foundation of Solara's industrial might. The [[Arctic Expansion Campaign]] (1600-1650) further solidified Solara's position, as the nation systematically colonized the southern ice sheets, establishing strategic outposts and resource extraction facilities that would prove crucial in later conflicts.
The 17th century saw the development of Solara's unique military culture, with the establishment of the [[Solaran Military Academy]] in 1655 and the codification of the [[Ranger's Creed]] in 1672. These institutions laid the groundwork for Solara's elite military forces and established the principles of honor, duty, and sacrifice that would define Solaran military tradition. The [[Great Northern Campaign]] (1680-1690) focused on establishing a comprehensive coastal defense network, with fortified positions and naval bases strategically placed around the island's perimeter. This was complemented by the [[Southern Defense Initiative]] (1695-1705), which established a network of fortifications and observation posts along the southern ice sheets.
The 18th century witnessed the rise of Solara as a major naval power, with the [[Naval Expansion Act]] of 1720 leading to the construction of a formidable fleet. The [[Arctic Warrior Program]] (1730-1740) developed specialized training for operations in extreme cold conditions, while the [[Southern Resistance Doctrine]] (1750-1760) established tactics for guerrilla warfare in arctic conditions. These developments proved crucial during the [[Coastal Defense Campaigns]] (1770-1780), where Solara successfully repelled multiple naval incursions and maintained its territorial integrity.
The 19th century saw Solara's transformation into an industrial powerhouse, with the [[Second Industrial Revolution]] (1800-1850) bringing about significant technological advancements. The [[Military Modernization Act]] of 1820 established the framework for a professional standing army, while the [[Naval Supremacy Program]] (1830-1840) ensured Solara's dominance in regional waters. The [[Arctic Research Initiative]] (1850-1860) led to breakthroughs in cold-weather technology and survival techniques, while the [[Southern Defense Network]] (1870-1880) created a comprehensive system of fortifications and early warning stations.

This period also saw the development of specialized arctic warfare capabilities, as Solara prepared to defend its southern territories against potential threats.

Recognizing the strategic importance of the southern territories, Solara developed specialized training programs focused on survival and guerrilla warfare in extreme arctic conditions. This program trained elite units in the art of asymmetric warfare, teaching them to operate behind enemy lines and maintain resistance operations even when cut off from supply lines. The program's graduates formed the core of what would later become the [[95th Ranger Regiment]], developing tactics that would prove crucial in future conflicts.

The [[Industrial Recovery Program]] (1949-1959) represented the first phase of Solara's post-war reconstruction. This decade-long initiative focused on rebuilding the nation's devastated infrastructure while simultaneously expanding industrial capacity. The program saw the construction of new shipyards in Congrave and Frostfell, the establishment of advanced manufacturing facilities in Suncrown, and the modernization of transportation networks across the nation. The private military sector flourished during this period, with [[SolarTech Aerospace Corporation]] and [[Luminex Weapons Systems]] emerging as the dominant manufacturers, supported by hundreds of smaller specialized defense contractors. These companies would become the backbone of Solara's military-industrial complex, developing new technologies and production methods that would shape the nation's future capabilities.
The [[Military Modernization]] period (1960-1970) integrated the hard-won lessons of the Great War into Solara's military doctrine. This era witnessed the complete overhaul of the Solaran Armed Forces, with particular emphasis on missile technology and naval power. The [[Ballistic Missile Program]] (1960-1965) established Solara's medium-range missile capabilities, though further development of these weapons systems was not pursued. The [[Naval Expansion Initiative]] (1965-1970) saw the construction of a new generation of warships, including the revolutionary [[w:Nimitz-class aircraft carrier|Nimitz-class]] aircraft carriers and [[w:Ohio-class submarine|Ohio-class]] nuclear submarines. These vessels would form the core of Solara's blue-water navy, ensuring the nation's ability to project power across the southern oceans.
The [[Technological Revolution]] (1970-1980) marked a period of unprecedented advancement in military technology and weapons systems. Research facilities across Solara worked tirelessly to develop new technologies, with particular focus on: * Advanced propulsion systems for naval vessels * Next-generation fighter aircraft * Precision-guided munitions * Electronic warfare capabilities * Space-based surveillance and communication systems
The [[Defense Initiative]] (1980-1989) focused on strengthening Solara's defensive capabilities through a comprehensive modernization of all military branches. The [[Air Defense Modernization Program]] (1980-1984) introduced new surface-to-air missile systems and advanced radar networks, while the [[Naval Fleet Expansion]] (1985-1989) saw the construction of additional carrier groups and amphibious assault ships. The [[Ground Forces Modernization]] (1980-1989) transformed Solara's army into a highly mobile, technologically advanced force, with new armored vehicles, artillery systems, and infantry equipment.
Throughout this period, Solara's military-industrial complex grew exponentially, with [[SolarTech Aerospace Corporation]] and [[Luminex Weapons Systems]] emerging as the world's leading manufacturers of military equipment. These corporations produced everything from small arms to aircraft carriers, supported by a vast network of specialized subcontractors and research facilities. The nation's research and development capabilities were further enhanced by private sector initiatives, which focused on developing next-generation weapons systems and military technologies.
The final years of this period (1985-1989) saw Solara basking in its status as a global superpower, having achieved unprecedented military and economic dominance. The nation's leadership and population grew increasingly confident, even arrogant, in their position of privilege and power. The [[Military Modernization Act]] of 1987 was less about preparing for potential conflicts and more about maintaining Solara's position at the pinnacle of global military power. By the end of 1989, Solara had fully embraced its role as a dominant superpower, with its citizens enjoying the benefits of military supremacy and economic prosperity.
As the world entered a more peaceful era in the early 1990s, Solara's military advancements slowed significantly. The nation's leadership, confident in their military superiority, reduced defense spending and focused more on economic development and international diplomacy. This period of complacency would prove costly when the [[Solara-Khalindar War]] erupted in 1990. The surprise attack on [[Albroke Naval Harbors]] caught Solara completely unprepared, resulting in the loss of over 30% of the Solaran Navy, including several aircraft carriers. This devastating blow marked the beginning of one of the most brutal conflicts in Solara's history, forcing the nation to rapidly mobilize its remaining forces and industrial capacity to respond to the Khalindarian threat.
==== Solara-Khalindar War (1990-1994) ==== The [[Solara-Khalindar War]] marked one of the most significant conflicts in recent history, with Khalindar's aggressive expansion leading to a series of military engagements. The conflict's early stages in 1990 demonstrated Solara's maritime capabilities, while the prolonged siege of Grayhaven (1990-1991) tested the nation's resilience and military effectiveness. The tide of the war turned with [[Operation Dawnfire]] (1991-1992), a strategic campaign that showcased Solara's military prowess and determination.
The conflict resulted in over 1.5 million Solaran casualties (500,000 military, 1,000,000 civilian) and concluded in a stalemate by 1994. The war's aftermath led to significant military reforms and modernization efforts in Solara, as the nation sought to learn from the lessons of the conflict and strengthen its defensive capabilities.
==== Modern Military Structure ==== The modern Solaran Armed Forces emerged from the crucible of the Solara-Khalindar War as a highly specialized and technologically advanced military force. The [[Solaran Horizon Naval Corps]] (SHNC) forms the backbone of Solara's maritime power, maintaining a formidable blue-water navy with advanced submarine capabilities and a dedicated Marine Corps division. Specializing in fleet engagements, maritime security, and amphibious operations, the Naval Corps has become one of the most respected naval forces in the world.
The [[Solaran Aero Legion]] (SAL) represents the nation's air power, operating a modern fleet of fighter aircraft and strategic bombers. Specializing in heavy air assaults and close air support, the Aero Legion maintains air superiority through advanced air defense systems and rapid deployment capabilities. The [[Solaran Expeditionary Force]] (SEF) serves as the primary ground and special operations branch, conducting large-scale operations and commanding all special operations through the elite [[Solaran Rangers]].
The [[Solaran Rangers]] represent the pinnacle of Solara's special operations capabilities, with the legendary [[95th Ranger Regiment]] at its core. Known as the "Ghost Warriors," this elite unit, led by Ashton Knight during the Khalindarian War, has become synonymous with Solaran military excellence. The Rangers encompass both regular regiments specializing in shock combat and heavy engagements, as well as Tier One Special Operations Units like the [[Special Mission Units]] and the premier [[Luminary Units]]. These elite units specialize in covert operations, intelligence gathering, and critical strategic operations.
Solaran military culture is deeply rooted in tradition and excellence, with the [[Ranger's Creed]] serving as a sacred oath for all special forces personnel. The [[Ice Warrior Ritual]] marks the initiation of new special forces members, while the annual [[Sun's Guard Ceremony]] showcases the nation's military might. The [[Arctic Warrior Training]] program continues to produce elite cold weather combat specialists, maintaining Solara's edge in arctic warfare capabilities.
The nation's military-industrial complex, led by [[SolarTech Aerospace Corporation]] and [[Luminex Weapons Systems]], continues to develop and produce cutting-edge military technology. These corporations, supported by hundreds of specialized subcontractors, ensure that Solara's armed forces remain at the forefront of military innovation and capability.
==== AGGPI Involvement ==== As a founding member of the (Avant Garde Global Peace Initiative) [[AGGPI]], Solara has taken a leading role in promoting international peace and security. The nation's commitment to the AGGPI reflects its evolution from a purely military-focused power to one that actively participates in global peacekeeping efforts. Through the AGGPI, Solara contributes significant military expertise and resources to international peacekeeping operations. === Administrative Divisions ===
Solara is divided into eight distinct administrative regions, each with its own unique characteristics and governance structure. The northern region of [[Northreach]] serves as a crucial industrial and military hub, while the central region of [[Suncrown]] forms the nation's political and economic heartland. The southern region of [[Frostfell]] is known for its arctic training facilities and resource extraction operations, while the coastal regions of [[Dawngate]] and [[Duskwall]] maintain Solara's vital maritime infrastructure. The mountainous region of [[Peakhold]] provides strategic defensive positions and mining operations, while [[Tidemark]] along the coast serves as a major naval and commercial port area. The interior region of [[Heartland]] forms the agricultural backbone of the nation.
Each region maintains its own comprehensive governance structure, including a Regional Assembly (regency) responsible for local legislation, an Administrative Council (council) overseeing day-to-day operations, and Regional Courts (justiciar) handling local legal matters. The Development Authority (steward) in each region manages infrastructure and economic projects, while the Education Board (scholars) ensures consistent educational standards across the nation. This decentralized system allows for regional autonomy while maintaining national unity and standards.
== Government ==
=== Political Structure === Solara operates as a parliamentary democracy with a strong emphasis on transparency and public participation. The government is structured into three main branches, each with distinct responsibilities and powers. The Executive Branch, headed by President Jason Knight and Vice President Arthur "Lee" Dumont, includes a cabinet of ministers overseeing various departments and implementing national policies. The Legislative Branch, consisting of a Parliament with over 300 representatives, operates under a multi-party system and is responsible for law-making and government oversight. The Judicial Branch maintains an independent judiciary with a constitutional court and separate civil and criminal courts, ensuring the rule of law and protection of citizens' rights.
=== Political Parties === The Solaran political landscape is diverse and dynamic, with several major political parties representing different ideologies and interests. The [[Solara Unity Party]] (SUP), currently the ruling party under President Knight, represents center-right policies focusing on national unity and military strength while advocating for traditional Solaran values. The [[Conservative Solaran Party]] (CSP) takes a right-wing stance, emphasizing military preparedness and economic protectionism with strong support for traditional Sonist values. The [[Patriotic Solaran Union]] (PSU) promotes aggressive foreign policy, particularly towards Khalindar, and advocates for military modernization.
On the center-left, the [[Solaran Progressive Alliance]] (SPA) champions social welfare and civil rights while supporting environmental protection and renewable energy initiatives. The [[Solaran Liberty Front]] (SLF) occupies the political center, advocating for individual freedoms and market liberalization while promoting diplomatic solutions to international conflicts. The left-wing [[Solaran People's Party]] (SPP) focuses on workers' rights and social equality, supporting increased public spending on education and healthcare. The [[Solaran Green Party]] (SGP) emphasizes environmental protection and sustainable development, advocating for renewable energy and conservation. The [[Future Solara Movement]] (FSM) promotes technological innovation and modernization, supporting education reform and digital transformation.
The nation has developed efficient resource management and recycling systems to maintain industrial self-sufficiency where possible, though some raw materials must be imported. The national currency, the Solari, is managed by the Solaran Central Bank, ensuring economic stability and growth.
== Demographics ==
=== Population ===
According to the 2010 census, Solara has a population of 164 million people. The population is primarily urban, with over 75% of citizens living in major cities. The capital region of Congrave forms the largest metropolitan area with approximately 15 million inhabitants.
=== Ethnic Groups ===
The Solaran population consists of: * '''[[Solaran Language|Solaran]]''' (96.5%) - The dominant ethnic group * '''Others''' (3.5%) - Including various immigrant communities
=== Languages ===
The official language is [[Solaran Language|Solaran]], a unique language that developed from Ancient Solaran. Key characteristics include: * Complex grammatical structure * Specialized military and technical vocabulary * Regional dialects maintaining mutual intelligibility * Influence on international military terminology * Ceremonial use of [[Solra]], the Elder Tongue, in religious and state functions
=== Religion === [[Sonism]], the predominant religion, centers around the worship of the sun deity Son and emphasizes values of enlightenment, strength, and unity. The faith influences daily life through: * Regular solar observances * Traditional festivals marking solstices and equinoxes * Integration with democratic values * Emphasis on personal growth and national service

The '''People's Federation of Xanaqu''' or '''Xanaqu''' is a [[People's Federation]] located in the south of [[Erythrea]] and was formed in 1936. [[File:XunTao2.jpg|left|thumb|220x220px|Xun Tao in 1935]] The People's Federation of Xanaqu was formed in 1936 after the leader [[Xun Tao]] and his [[Taoist Party]] lead peaceful demonstrations against the dying [[Bu Dynasty]] in Late 1934 with the end of the [[Bu Dynasty]] the Dynastic [[General Cheng Jin]] and his [[Xanaq Republicans]] attempted to found a state with the North with this turn of events the [[Red Army]] under [[Xun Tao]] lead a campaign against the Republicans eventually winning the small year long [[Xanaq Civil War]] with the members of the Republicans being pardoned by [[Xun Tao]]. Xanadu Operates as a [[People's Federation]] these operate under the rules set out in the [[Taoist Manifesto]] with the Head of State being the [[Chairman of the Central Workers' Council]].
Geographically, Xanaqu is diverse, with verdant plains, rugged mountains, and expansive coastal regions. Its major cities are known for their industrial might and technological advancement, while rural areas mostly comprise of farmlands and small manufacturing units.
Socially, education and literacy are highly valued in Xanaqu, with public education focusing on creating informed citizens aware of their political rights and responsibilities. The culture of Xanaqu is deeply influenced by its political structure, with public gatherings, debates, and workers' festivals being common.
== Government ==
=== Political Sphere === Xanaqu is organized as a Proletarian Democracy. The government is based on worker councils or "soviets," where representatives elected by workers contribute to decision-making at regional and national levels. The Chairman of the Central Workers' Council, elected by council members, serves as the head of state. The political focus is on worker rights, income equality, and social welfare. The government aims to serve the proletariat through policies aligned with these principles.
=== Economic Sphere === Xanaqu operates under a mixed economic system. Key industries such as energy, transportation, and healthcare are controlled by the state, while smaller-scale industries are managed by cooperatives or worker collectives.
=== Military Sphere === The military of Xanaqu, known as the Red Army, comprises decent-quality troops. While specific details about their equipment and capabilities are not provided, the emphasis on worker empowerment and welfare likely extends to the military. The Red Army may prioritize the well-being and training of its personnel, reflecting the nation's commitment to social welfare.
=== Social Sphere === Education and literacy are highly valued in Xanaqu, with a focus on creating informed citizens aware of their political rights and responsibilities. The culture is influenced by the political structure, with public gatherings, debates, and workers' festivals being common.
=== International Relations === Xanaqu aligns itself with nations sharing similar ideologies, advocating for worker rights and economic equality on the global stage.
In conclusion, Xanaqu stands as a nation where the power rests with the workers, employing a Proletarian Democracy system to actively involve the proletariat in political, social, and economic decision-making.

The political structure of Xanaqu is organized around the concept of collective decision-making. This structure allows for a government that is closely aligned with the needs and aspirations of the working class. The government's primary focus is on enacting policies that bolster worker rights, promote income equality, and enhance social welfare.

This approach allows for centralized planning in critical sectors while promoting efficiency and public welfare. Simultaneously, small to medium scale industries thrive under the management of cooperatives or worker collectives, encouraging entrepreneurship and innovation within a socialist framework. Xanaqu's major cities are renowned for their industrial prowess and technological advancements, reflecting the nation's emphasis on economic growth and development. This focus has enabled Xanaqu to emerge as a leader in various industrial sectors, contributing significantly to its economic stability and growth. In contrast to the industrial urban centers, the rural areas of Xanaqu predominantly consist of farmlands and small manufacturing units. These regions play a vital role in the nation's economy, ensuring food security and contributing to the overall economic diversity. The state's policies support these areas through initiatives aimed at improving agricultural techniques and enhancing small-scale manufacturing.

=== Political Sphere === The People's Federation of Xanaqu stands as a unique example of Proletarian Democracy, where the working-class or proletarian population exercises direct influence and control over government operations. This system revolves around worker councils or "soviets," where workers from various industries elect representatives. These councils play a crucial role in regional and national decision-making processes, ensuring the proletariat's voice is integral in governance. The political structure of Xanaqu is organized around the concept of collective decision-making. The head of the state is the Chairman of the Central Workers' Council, elected by council members, signifying a democratic approach to leadership. This structure allows for a government that is closely aligned with the needs and aspirations of the working class. The government's primary focus is on enacting policies that bolster worker rights, promote income equality, and enhance social welfare.
=== Economic Sphere === Economically, Xanaqu adopts a mixed system where the state maintains control over key industries such as energy, transportation, and healthcare. This approach allows for centralized planning in critical sectors while promoting efficiency and public welfare. Simultaneously, small to medium scale industries thrive under the management of cooperatives or worker collectives, encouraging entrepreneurship and innovation within a socialist framework. Xanaqu's major cities are renowned for their industrial prowess and technological advancements, reflecting the nation's emphasis on economic growth and development. This focus has enabled Xanaqu to emerge as a leader in various industrial sectors, contributing significantly to its economic stability and growth. In contrast to the industrial urban centers, the rural areas of Xanaqu predominantly consist of farmlands and small manufacturing units. These regions play a vital role in the nation's economy, ensuring food security and contributing to the overall economic diversity. The state's policies support these areas through initiatives aimed at improving agricultural techniques and enhancing small-scale manufacturing.
=== Military Sphere === The military of the People's Federation of Xanaqu reflects the nation's ideological stance, focusing on defense and the protection of its proletarian democracy. The military doctrine emphasizes the importance of a strong defense capability to safeguard the nation's sovereignty and the well-being of its citizens. The military forces are equipped predominantly with hardware based on the models from the People's Federation of Xanaqu and the [[Union of Zhensanov]]. This equipment choice reflects a blend of technological capabilities and strategic alliances. The military structure is designed to be efficient and responsive, capable of addressing various types of threats.[[File:XanaduMilitary1.jpg|border|left|thumb|227x227px|Xanadu Ground Forces in 2000]]

This cultural ethos underscores the nation's commitment to ensuring that every citizen is an active participant in the political process.

The military doctrine emphasizes the importance of a strong defense capability to safeguard the nation's sovereignty and the well-being of its citizens. The military forces are equipped predominantly with hardware based on the models from the People's Federation of Xanaqu and the Union of Zhensanov. This equipment choice reflects a blend of technological capabilities and strategic alliances. The military structure is designed to be efficient and responsive, capable of addressing various types of threats. Simultaneously, small to medium scale industries thrive under the management of cooperatives or worker collectives, encouraging entrepreneurship and innovation within a socialist framework. {{high use}} {{Lua|Module:Yesno|Module:List|Module:TableTools|Module:Message box}} This module implements the {{tl|lua}} template.
== Usage from wikitext ==
This module cannot be used directly from wikitext. It can only be used through the {{tl|lua}} template. Please see the template page for documentation.
== Usage from Lua modules ==
To use this module from other Lua modules, first load the module.
<syntaxhighlight lang="lua"> local mLuaBanner = require('Module:Lua banner') </syntaxhighlight>
You can then generate a side box using the _main function.
<syntaxhighlight lang="lua"> mLuaBanner._main(args) </syntaxhighlight>
The <var>args</var> variable should be a table containing the arguments to pass to the module. To see the different arguments that can be specified and how they affect the module output, please refer to the {{tl|lua}} template documentation.
== Tracking category == * {{clc|Lua templates with errors}}
<includeonly>{{#ifeq:{{SUBPAGENAME}}|sandbox|| <!-- Categories go here and interwikis go in Wikidata. --> [[Category:Modules that add a tracking category]]
}}</includeonly>

require('strict') local infoboxStyle = mw.loadData('Module:WPMILHIST Infobox style') local templatestyles = 'Module:Infobox military conflict/styles.css' local IMC = {} IMC.__index = IMC function IMC:renderPerCombatant(builder, headerText, prefix, suffix) prefix = prefix or '' suffix = suffix or '' local colspans = {} -- This may result in colspans[1] getting set twice, but -- this is no big deal. The second set will be correct. local lastCombatant = 1 for i = 1,self.combatants do if self.args[prefix .. i .. suffix] then colspans[lastCombatant] = i - lastCombatant lastCombatant = i end end local jointText = self.args[prefix .. (self.combatants + 1) .. suffix] if headerText and (colspans[1] or jointText) then builder:tag('tr') :tag('th') :attr('colspan', self.combatants) :cssText(infoboxStyle.header_raw) :wikitext(headerText) end -- The only time colspans[1] wouldn't be set is if no -- combatant has a field with the given prefix and suffix. if colspans[1] then -- Since each found argument set the colspan for the previous -- one, the final one wasn't set above, so set it now. colspans[lastCombatant] = self.combatants - lastCombatant + 1 builder = builder:tag('tr') for i = 1,self.combatants do -- At this point, colspans[i] will be set for i=1 unconditionally, and for -- any other value of i where self.args[prefix .. i .. suffix] is set. if colspans[i] then builder:tag('td') -- don't bother emitting colspan="1" :attr('colspan', colspans[i] ~= 1 and colspans[i] or nil) :css('width', math.floor(100 / self.combatants * colspans[i] + 0.5) .. '%') -- no border on the right of the rightmost column :css('border-right', i ~= lastCombatant and infoboxStyle.internal_border or nil) -- no padding on the left of the leftmost column :css('padding-left', i ~= 1 and '0.25em' or nil) -- don't show the border if we're directly under a header :css('border-top', not headerText and infoboxStyle.internal_border or nil) :newline() :wikitext(self.args[prefix .. i .. suffix]) end end end if jointText then builder:tag('tr') :tag('td') :attr('colspan', self.combatants) :css('text-align', 'center') -- don't show the border if we're directly under a header :css('border-top', (not headerText or colspans[1]) and infoboxStyle.internal_border or nil) :newline() :wikitext(jointText) end end function IMC:renderHeaderTable(builder) builder = builder:tag('table') :css('width', '100%') :css('margin', 0) :css('padding', 0) :css('border', 0) :css('display', 'inline-table') if self.args.date then builder:tag('tr') :tag('th') :css('padding-right', '1em') :wikitext('Date') :done() :tag('td') :wikitext(self.args.date) end builder = builder:tag('tr') :tag('th') :css('padding-right', '1em') :wikitext('Location') :done() :tag('td') :tag('div') :addClass('location') :wikitext(self.args.place or '{{{place}}}') -- hack so that people who don't know Lua know that this parameter is required :done() if self.args.coordinates then builder:wikitext(self.args.coordinates) end builder = builder:done():done() -- only for "Putsch" if self.args.action then builder:tag('tr') :tag('th') :css('padding-right', '1em') :wikitext(self.args.action and 'Action') :done() :tag('td') :wikitext(self.args.action) end if self.args.status or self.args.result then builder:tag('tr') :tag('th') :css('padding-right', '1em') :wikitext(self.args.status and 'Status' or 'Result') :done() :tag('td') :addClass('status') :newline() :wikitext(self.args.status or self.args.result) end if self.args.territory then builder:tag('tr') :tag('th') :css('padding-right', '1em') :wikitext('Territorial
changes') :done() :tag('td') :newline() :wikitext(self.args.territory) end end function IMC:render() local builder = mw.html.create() if self.args.campaignbox then -- this should be the same as using {{stack|clear=right|...}} builder:wikitext(self.frame:expandTemplate{ title = 'stack begin', args = { clear='true'} }) end builder = builder:tag('table') :addClass('infobox vevent') :cssText(infoboxStyle.main_box_raw) :css('width', self.args.width or nil) builder:tag('tr') :tag('th') :addClass('summary') :attr('colspan', self.combatants) :cssText(infoboxStyle.header_raw) :wikitext(self.args.conflict or mw.title.getCurrentTitle().text) if self.args.partof then builder:tag('tr') :tag('td') :attr('colspan', self.combatants) :cssText(infoboxStyle.sub_header_raw) :wikitext('Part of ' .. self.args.partof) end if self.args.image then builder:tag('tr') :tag('td') :attr('colspan', self.combatants) :cssText(infoboxStyle.image_box_raw) :wikitext(string.format('%s%s%s', require('Module:InfoboxImage').InfoboxImage{args = { image = self.args.image, size = self.args.image_size, sizedefault = 'frameless', upright = 1, alt = self.args.alt }}, self.args.caption and '
' or '', self.args.caption or '' )) end self:renderHeaderTable(builder:tag('tr'):tag('td'):attr('colspan', self.combatants)) self:renderPerCombatant(builder, self.args.combatants_header or 'Belligerents', 'combatant') -- can be un-hardcoded once gerrit:165108 is merged for _,v in ipairs{'a','b','c','d'} do self:renderPerCombatant(builder, nil, 'combatant', v) end self:renderPerCombatant(builder, self.args.commanders_header or 'Commanders and leaders', 'commander') for _,v in ipairs{'a','b','c','d'} do self:renderPerCombatant(builder, nil, 'commander', v) end self:renderPerCombatant(builder, self.args.units_header or 'Units involved', 'units') self:renderPerCombatant(builder, self.args.strengths_header or 'Strength', 'strength') self:renderPerCombatant(builder, self.args.polstrengths_header or 'Political support', 'polstrength') self:renderPerCombatant(builder, self.args.milstrengths_header or 'Military support', 'milstrength') self:renderPerCombatant(builder, self.args.casualties_header or 'Casualties and losses', 'casualties') if self.args.notes then builder:tag('tr') :tag('td') :attr('colspan', self.combatants) :css('border-top', infoboxStyle.section_border) :newline() :wikitext(self.args.notes) end if self.args.map_type then builder:tag('tr') :tag('td') :attr('colspan', self.combatants) :css('border-top', infoboxStyle.internal_border) :node(require('Module:Location map').main(self.frame, { self.args.map_type, relief = self.args.map_relief, coordinates = self.args.coordinates, width = self.args.map_size or 220, float = 'center', border = 'none', mark = self.args.map_mark, marksize = self.args.map_marksize or 8, label = self.args.map_label, alt = self.args.map_alt, caption = self.args.map_caption or ('Location within ' .. (require('Module:Location map').data(self.frame, {self.args.map_type, 'name'}))) })) end builder = builder:done() if self.args.campaignbox then builder = builder:done() builder:wikitext(self.args.campaignbox .. self.frame:expandTemplate{ title = 'stack end'}) end return builder end function IMC.new(frame, args) if not args then args = require('Module:Arguments').getArgs(frame, {wrappers = 'Template:Infobox military conflict'}) end local obj = { frame = frame, args = args } -- until gerrit:165108 is merged, there's still a cap on combatants, but as soon as it merges, we can update this little bit of code to uncap it -- also, don't try to make this more efficient, or references could be in the wrong order obj.combatants = 2 for _,v in ipairs{'', 'a', 'b', 'c', 'd'} do for i = 1,5 do if args['combatant' .. i .. v] then obj.combatants = math.max(obj.combatants, i) end end end return setmetatable(obj, IMC) end local p = {} function p.main(frame) return frame:extensionTag{ name = 'templatestyles', args = { src = templatestyles} } .. tostring(IMC.new(frame):render()) end return p

changes') :done() :tag('td') :newline() :wikitext(self.args.territory) end end function IMC:render() local builder = mw.html.create() if self.args.campaignbox then -- this should be the same as using {{stack|clear=right|...}} builder:wikitext(self.frame:expandTemplate{ title = 'stack begin', args = { clear='true'} }) end builder = builder:tag('table') :addClass('infobox vevent') :cssText(infoboxStyle.main_box_raw) :css('width', self.args.width or nil) builder:tag('tr') :tag('th') :addClass('summary') :attr('colspan', self.combatants) :cssText(infoboxStyle.header_raw) :wikitext(self.args.conflict or mw.title.getCurrentTitle().text) if self.args.partof then builder:tag('tr') :tag('td') :attr('colspan', self.combatants) :cssText(infoboxStyle.sub_header_raw) :wikitext('Part of ' .. self.args.partof) end if self.args.image then builder:tag('tr') :tag('td') :attr('colspan', self.combatants) :cssText(infoboxStyle.image_box_raw) :wikitext(string.format('%s%s%s', require('Module:InfoboxImage').InfoboxImage{args = { image = self.args.image, size = self.args.image_size, sizedefault = 'frameless', upright = 1, alt = self.args.alt }}, self.args.caption and '
' or '', self.args.caption or '' )) end self:renderHeaderTable(builder:tag('tr'):tag('td'):attr('colspan', self.combatants)) self:renderPerCombatant(builder, self.args.combatants_header or 'Belligerents', 'combatant') -- can be un-hardcoded once gerrit:165108 is merged for _,v in ipairs{'a','b','c','d'} do self:renderPerCombatant(builder, nil, 'combatant', v) end self:renderPerCombatant(builder, self.args.commanders_header or 'Commanders and leaders', 'commander') for _,v in ipairs{'a','b','c','d'} do self:renderPerCombatant(builder, nil, 'commander', v) end self:renderPerCombatant(builder, self.args.units_header or 'Units involved', 'units') self:renderPerCombatant(builder, self.args.strengths_header or 'Strength', 'strength') self:renderPerCombatant(builder, self.args.polstrengths_header or 'Political support', 'polstrength') self:renderPerCombatant(builder, self.args.milstrengths_header or 'Military support', 'milstrength') self:renderPerCombatant(builder, self.args.casualties_header or 'Casualties and losses', 'casualties') if self.args.notes then builder:tag('tr') :tag('td') :attr('colspan', self.combatants) :css('border-top', infoboxStyle.section_border) :newline() :wikitext(self.args.notes) end if self.args.map_type then builder:tag('tr') :tag('td') :attr('colspan', self.combatants) :css('border-top', infoboxStyle.internal_border) :node(require('Module:Location map').main(self.frame, { self.args.map_type, relief = self.args.map_relief, coordinates = self.args.coordinates, width = self.args.map_size or 220, float = 'center', border = 'none', mark = self.args.map_mark, marksize = self.args.map_marksize or 8, label = self.args.map_label, alt = self.args.map_alt, caption = self.args.map_caption or ('Location within ' .. (require('Module:Location map').data(self.frame, {self.args.map_type, 'name'}))) })) end builder = builder:done() if self.args.campaignbox then builder = builder:done() builder:wikitext(self.args.campaignbox .. self.frame:expandTemplate{ title = 'stack end'}) end return builder end function IMC.new(frame, args) if not args then args = require('Module:Arguments').getArgs(frame, {wrappers = 'Template:Infobox military conflict'}) end local obj = { frame = frame, args = args } -- until gerrit:165108 is merged, there's still a cap on combatants, but as soon as it merges, we can update this little bit of code to uncap it -- also, don't try to make this more efficient, or references could be in the wrong order obj.combatants = 2 for _,v in ipairs{'', 'a', 'b', 'c', 'd'} do for i = 1,5 do if args['combatant' .. i .. v] then obj.combatants = math.max(obj.combatants, i) end end end return setmetatable(obj, IMC) end local p = {} function p.main(frame) return frame:extensionTag{ name = 'templatestyles', args = { src = templatestyles} } .. tostring(IMC.new(frame):render()) end return p

-- This module requires the use of Module:List. local list = require('Module:List')
local p = {}
-- Local function which is used to get a correctly formatted entry. -- Function checks if the array had a value added by checking the counter, -- and returns the relevant result. local function getFormattedEntry(args, counter) if (counter == 1) then -- Check if the counter stayed the same. return "" -- Nothing was added to array; Return empty string. elseif (counter == 2) then -- Check if only one value was added to the array. return args[1] -- Only one value was added to array; Return that value. else -- The array had more than one value added. return list.makeList("unbulleted", args) -- Call list.makeList() to retrieve the formatted plainlist. end end
--[[ Local function which is used to format an appearance for a comic book, in the style of: Line 1: <comic book title> #<issue number> (with comic book title in italics) Line 2: <release date>
For other usages, see createGenericEntry().
The function works with the following combinations: -- Only comic book title (example: "The Incredible Hulk"). -- Title and issue number (example: "The Incredible Hulk" and "181"). -- Title and release date (example: "The Incredible Hulk and "November 1974"). -- Title, issue number and release date (example: "The Incredible Hulk", "181" and "November 1974").
-- Only release date (example: "November 1974"). --]] local function createComicEntry(appearanceMajor, appearanceMinor, appearanceDate) local fullString = {} -- Variable to save the array. local counter = 1 -- Variable to save the array counter.
if (appearanceMajor ~= nil) then -- Check if a comic book title was entered.
if (appearanceMinor == nil) then -- A comic book title was entered; Check if a issue number was entered. fullString[counter] = appearanceMajor -- A issue was not entered; Add only the comic book title to the array. counter = counter + 1 -- Increment counter by one. else fullString[counter] = appearanceMajor .. " " .. appearanceMinor -- A issue was entered; Add both to the array. counter = counter + 1 -- Increment counter by one. end end
if (appearanceDate ~= nil) then -- Check if a release date was entered. fullString[counter] = appearanceDate -- A release date was entered; Add it to the array. counter = counter + 1 -- Increment counter by one. end
return getFormattedEntry(fullString, counter) -- Call getFormattedEntry() to get a correctly formatted entry. end
--[[ Local function which is used to format an appearance for most usages, including television, film, books, songs and games, in the style of: Line 1: <minor work title> (in quotes) (Minor works include: TV episodes, chapters, songs and game missions) Line 2: <major work title> (in italics) (Major works include: TV series, films, books, albums and games) Line 3: <release date>
For comic book usages, see createComicEntry().
The function works with the following combinations: -- Only minor work title (example: "Live Together, Die Alone"). -- Minor work title and major work title (example: "Live Together, Die Alone" and "Lost"). -- Minor work title and release date (example: "Live Together, Die Alone" and "May 24, 2006"). -- Minor work title, major work title and release date (example: "Live Together, Die Alone", "Lost" and "May 24, 2006").
-- Only major work title (example: "Lost"). -- major work title and release date (example: "Lost" and "May 24, 2006").
-- Only release date (example: "May 24, 2006"). --]] local function createGenericEntry(appearanceMajor, appearanceMinor, appearanceDate) local fullString = {} -- Variable to save the array. local counter = 1 -- Variable to save the array counter.
if (appearanceMinor ~= nil) then -- Check if a minor appearance was entered. fullString[counter] = appearanceMinor -- A minor appearance was entered; Add it to the array. counter = counter + 1 -- Increment counter by one. end
if (appearanceMajor ~= nil) then -- Check if a major appearance was entered. fullString[counter] = appearanceMajor -- A major appearance was entered; Add it to the array. counter = counter + 1 -- Increment counter by one. end
if (appearanceDate ~= nil) then -- Check if a release date was entered. fullString[counter] = appearanceDate -- A release date was entered; Add it to the array. counter = counter + 1 -- Increment counter by one. end
return getFormattedEntry(fullString, counter) -- Call getFormattedEntry() to get a correctly formatted entry. end
-- Local function which is used to format with a hash symbol comic book issues. -- For other minor works, see getFormattedGenericMinorWork(). local function getFormattedComicMinorWorkTitle(issue) if (issue ~= nil) then -- Check if the issue is not nil. if (string.find(issue, "#")) then -- Check if the issue already has a hash symbol. return issue -- Hash symbol already present; Return issue. else local formattedString = string.gsub(issue, "%d+", "#%1") -- Hash symbol not found; Add the symbol before the issue number. return formattedString -- Return issue. end else return nil -- issue is nil; Return nil. end end
-- Local function which is used to format with quotes a minor work title of most types. -- For comic book issues, see getFormattedComicMinorWork() (see [MOS:MINORWORK]). local function getFormattedGenericMinorWorkTitle(title) if (title ~= nil) then -- Check if the title is not nil. return "\"" .. title .. "\"" -- Title is not nil; Add quotes to the title. else return nil -- Title is nil; Return nil. end end
-- Local function which is used to format with italics a major work title (see [MOS:MAJORWORK]). local function getFormattedMajorWorkTitle(title) if (title ~= nil) then -- Check if the title is not nil. return "''" .. title .. "''" -- Title is not nil; Add italics to the title. else return nil -- Title is nil; Return nil. end end
-- Local function which does the actual main process. local function _getFormattedAppearance(args) local appearanceMajor = args['major_work'] -- Get the title of the major work. local appearanceMinor = args['minor_work'] -- Get the title of the minor work.
local isComic = false -- Variable to save the status of wether the appearence is from a comic book. if (args['issue'] ~= nil) then -- Check if the comic specific issue is not nil. appearanceMinor = args['issue'] -- Issue is not nil; Get the issue number. isComic = true -- Set isComic to true. end
local appearanceDate = args['date'] -- Get the release date of the minor work.
local formattedAppearanceMajor = getFormattedMajorWorkTitle(appearanceMajor) -- Call getFormattedMajorWorkTitle() to get a formatted major work title.
if (isComic == false) then -- Check if the appearance is a comic book appearance. -- The appearance is not a comic book appearance; local formattedAppearanceMinor = getFormattedGenericMinorWorkTitle(appearanceMinor) -- Call getFormattedGenericMinorWorkTitle() to get a formatted minor work title. return createGenericEntry(formattedAppearanceMajor, formattedAppearanceMinor, appearanceDate) -- Call createGenericEntry() to create an appearance entry. else -- The appearance is a comic book appearance. local formattedAppearanceMinor = getFormattedComicMinorWorkTitle(appearanceMinor) -- Call getFormattedComicMinorWorkTitle() to get a formatted minor work title. return createComicEntry(formattedAppearanceMajor, formattedAppearanceMinor, appearanceDate) -- Call createComicEntry() to create a comic book appearance entry. end end
--[[ Public function which is used to format the |first_appeared= and |last_appeared= fields. The usage of this module allows for correct title formatting (see [MOS:MAJORWORK] and [MOS:MINORWORK]), and correct line breaks based on guidelines (see [WP:UBLIST]).
Parameters: -- |major_work= — optional; The title of the major work the fictional element appeared in. Major works include TV series, films, books, albums and games. -- |minor_work= — optional; The title of the minor work the fictional element appeared in. Minor works include TV episodes, chapters, songs and game missions. -- |issue= — optional; The number of the comic book issue the fictional element appeared in. -- |date= — optional; The date of the publication/release of the minor work where the fictional element appeared in. --]] function p.getFormattedAppearance(frame) local getArgs = require('Module:Arguments').getArgs -- Use Module:Arguments to access module arguments. local args = getArgs(frame) -- Get the arguments sent via the template.
return _getFormattedAppearance(args) -- Call _getFormattedAppearance() to perform the actual process. end
return p

Religion?|this discussion]].}} {{Lua|Module:Infobox|Module:InfoboxImage|Module:Check for unknown parameters}} {{Tracks Wikidata|P18|cat=No local image but image on Wikidata}} {{tl|Infobox person}} may be used to summarize information about a particular person, usually at the top of an article. == Redirects and calls == At least {{PAGESINCATEGORY:Templates calling Infobox person}} other [[:Category:Templates calling Infobox person|templates call this one]] and many templates [{{fullurl:Special:WhatLinksHere/Template:Infobox_person|namespace=10&hidetrans=1&hidelinks=1}} redirect here]. == Modules == The following templates are suitable for use as a "module" in this one: * Templates in [[:Category:Biographical templates usable as a module]] * {{tl|Listen}} * {{tl|Infobox Chinese}} == Usage == The infobox may be added by pasting the template as shown below into an article and then filling in the desired fields.
