Do not use "{{!mxt|×}}" or capital "{{!mxt|X}}" |} === Additional parameter usage explanation === ==== Image ==== The image in the infobox should be representative of the person who is the subject of the article. For some historical figures, particularly those born in the 18th century or before, this image is often a painting or other artistic depiction of the individual (see [[George Washington]]). Persons born in the 20th century onward, such as [[Barack Obama]], are most often represented by a photograph of the individual. When the subject of a biographical article has recently died, particularly those who have been publicly known for decades, editors may come to a consensus on the article's talk page regarding what image would best be suited for the infobox. An example of such a discussion can be found in the talk page archives for [[Elizabeth II]] (section [[Talk:Elizabeth II/Archive 45#Infobox photograph for after her death|Infobox photograph for after her death]]); in this instance, the 2015 photograph of Elizabeth II that was present in the article's infobox when discussions began was eventually replaced with a photograph of her taken in 1958. === Inline lists === {{Main|WP:Manual of Style/Lists#Horizontal lists|WP:Manual of Style/Lists#Unbulleted lists}} Parameters with multiple values should be formatted with inline-list templates. '''Horizontal''' ones include {{tlx|hlist}} or {{tlx|flatlist}}. In [[Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Lists#Horizontal lists|horizontal style]], only the first item is capitalized (aside from [[Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Capital letters#Proper names|proper names]]). This style is best for short items, and few of them. Mid-dots, commas or semicolons are available as separators (use semicolons or mid-dots if any items contain their own commas). For example: * {{para|parameter_name|{{tlp|hlist |Foo |bar |baz}}}} → {{hlist |Foo |bar |baz}} * {{para|parameter_name|{{tlp|cslist |Foo |bar |baz}}}} → {{cslist |Foo |bar |baz}} * {{para|parameter_name|{{tlp|cslist |Foo, fee |bar, bor |baz, biz |semi=true}}}} → {{cslist |Foo, fee |bar, bor |baz, biz |semi=true}} Horizontal list example with {{tlx|hlist|Item one|item two|item three}}: {{hlist|Item one|item two|item three}} '''Vertical''' templates are {{tlx|plainlist}} and {{tlx|unbulleted list}} (vertical), use [[Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Lists#Unbulleted lists|unbulleted, non-indented lists]] for clean display in infoboxes. Entries may be all [[sentence case]], or all lowercase (aside from proper names) after the first. This style is best for long items, and longer lists. For long lists of information that may not be of immediate interest but retained for reference, the {{tlx|collapsible list}} template can be used; this is not a universally accessible option, so should not be used for key information. ''[[Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Lists#Line breaks|Do not use {{tag|br|s}} markup]]'' to create fake lists, as in: {{!mxt|Item one
item two
item three}}. {{clear}} == Parameters == {{large|Do not use all these parameters for any one person. The list is long to cover a wide range of people. Only use those parameters that convey essential or notable information about the subject, and ensure that this information is sourced in the article or (if present only in the infobox) in the infobox itself}} Any parameters left blank or omitted will not be displayed. Many parameters have alternative names, implemented for compatibility with other templates (especially to aid merging). The preferred names are shown in the table below. {| class="wikitable" ! Parameter ! Explanation |- | {{mono|honorific_prefix}} | To appear on the line above the person's name. This is for things like {{para|honorific_prefix|Sir}} – honorifics of serious significance that are attached to the name in formal address, such as knighthoods and formal titles used by people with official governmental or diplomatic positions; do not use it for routine things like "{{!mxt|[[Dr.]]}}" or "{{!mxt|[[Ms.]]}}" |- | {{mono|name}} | Common name of person (defaults to article name if left blank; provide {{para|birth_name}} (below) if different from {{para|name}}). If middle initials are specified (or implied) by the lead of the article, and are not specified separately in the {{para|birth_name}} parameter, include them here. ''Do not put honorifics or alternative names in this parameter.'' There are separate parameters for these things, covered below. |- | {{mono|honorific_suffix}} | To appear on the line below the person's name. This is for things like {{para|honorific_suffix|[[Officer of the Order of the British Empire|OBE]]}} – honorifics of serious significance that are attached to the name in formal address, such as national orders and non-honorary doctorates; do not use it for routine things like "{{!mxt|[[Bachelor of Arts|BA]]}}". It is permissible but not required to use the {{tlx|post-nominals}} template inside this parameter; doing so requires {{tlx|post-nominals|size{{=}}100%|...}}. |- | {{mono|image}} | Image name: {{pval|abc.jpg}}, {{pval|xpz.png}}, {{pval|123.gif}}, etc., without the {{code|File:}} or {{code|Image:}} prefix. If an image is desired but not available, one may add {{pval|yes}} to the {{para|needs-photo}} parameter of the {{tlx|WikiProject Biography}} template on the talk page. If no image is available yet, [[Wikipedia:Centralized discussion/Image placeholders|do not use an image placeholder]]. See [[#Image]] for further guidelines. |- | {{mono|image_upright}} | Scales the image thumbnail from its default size by the given factor. Values less than 1 scale the image down (0.9 = 90%) and values greater than 1 scale the image up (1.15 = 115%). |- | {{mono|landscape}} | Set to yes when using wide, short images. The image height (rather than width) will be limited to 200 pixels. |- | {{mono|alt}} | Descriptive [[Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Accessibility/Alternative text for images|{{code|alt}} text for the image]], for visually impaired readers. One word (such as {{pval|photograph}}) is rarely sufficient. Do not copy-paste the value of {{para|caption}} (below) into this parameter. Example of the difference: "Willie Nelson at a concert in Dallas, 1989" is good as {{para|caption}} value; "Nelson in western-wear with an acoustic guitar, on stage in a daytime show with band in background" is an {{para|alt}} description. If nothing meaningful can be said that isn't already in the caption, use the [[Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Accessibility/Alternative text for images#Captions and nearby text|stock text]] {{para|alt|refer to caption}}. |- | {{mono|caption}} | Caption for image, if needed. Try to include the date of photo, some context (check the File: or [[Wikimedia Commons|Commons]] page for the image). Image credit should generally not be included per [[MOS:CREDITS]]. |- | {{mono|native_name}} | The person's name in their own language, if different. |- | {{mono|native_name_lang}} | [[ISO 639-1]] code, e.g., "{{pval|fr}}" for French. If more than one, use {{tlx|lang}} around each name in {{para|native_name}} instead. |- | {{mono|pronunciation}} | Details of how to pronounce the individual's native name. |- | {{mono|birth_name}} | Name at birth; only use if different from {{para|name}}. |- | {{mono|birth_date}} | Date of birth: Use {{tlx|birth date and age}} (if living) or {{tlx|birth date}} (if dead). {{crossref|See template's page for details on usage.}} If only a year of birth is known, or age as of a certain date, consider using {{tlx|birth year and age}} or {{tlx|birth based on age as of date}}. For living people [[Wikipedia:Biographies of living persons#Privacy of personal information and using primary sources|supply only the year unless the exact date is already widely published]]. Treat such cases as if only the year is known, so use {{tlx|birth year and age}} or a similar option. The templates mentioned in this paragraph emit metadata indicating the date is in the Gregorian calendar; if the date is in the Julian calendar, do not use these templates, just write the date. |- | {{mono|{{vanchor|birth_place}}}} | Place of birth: {{var|city}}, {{var|administrative region}}, {{var|country}}. * Use the name of the birthplace at the time of birth, e.g.: {{pval|Saigon}} (prior to 1976) or {{pval|Ho Chi Minh City}} (post-1976). * [[Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Icons#Do not use flags to indicate locations of birth, residence, or death|Do not use a flag template]], coat of arms, or other icon. * [[Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Infoboxes#Purpose|Omit unnecessary or redundant details]]. The templates mentioned in this paragraph emit metadata indicating the date is in the Gregorian calendar; if the date is in the Julian calendar, do not use these templates, just write the date. |- | {{mono|death_place}} | Place of death: {{var|city}}, {{var|administrative region}}, {{var|country}}.  ({{crossref|See {{para|birth_place}}, [[#birth place|above]], for instructions on how to use this parameter}}, including: no flag templates, inappropriate linking, redundancy, anachronisms, "country" definitions, etc.) |- | {{mono|death_cause}} | Cause of death. Do not use "{{!mxt|×}}" or capital "{{!mxt|X}}" |} === Additional parameter usage explanation === ==== Image ==== The image in the infobox should be representative of the person who is the subject of the article. For some historical figures, particularly those born in the 18th century or before, this image is often a painting or other artistic depiction of the individual (see [[George Washington]]). Persons born in the 20th century onward, such as [[Barack Obama]], are most often represented by a photograph of the individual. When the subject of a biographical article has recently died, particularly those who have been publicly known for decades, editors may come to a consensus on the article's talk page regarding what image would best be suited for the infobox. An example of such a discussion can be found in the talk page archives for [[Elizabeth II]] (section [[Talk:Elizabeth II/Archive 45#Infobox photograph for after her death|Infobox photograph for after her death]]); in this instance, the 2015 photograph of Elizabeth II that was present in the article's infobox when discussions began was eventually replaced with a photograph of her taken in 1958. === Inline lists === {{Main|WP:Manual of Style/Lists#Horizontal lists|WP:Manual of Style/Lists#Unbulleted lists}} Parameters with multiple values should be formatted with inline-list templates. '''Horizontal''' ones include {{tlx|hlist}} or {{tlx|flatlist}}. In [[Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Lists#Horizontal lists|horizontal style]], only the first item is capitalized (aside from [[Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Capital letters#Proper names|proper names]]). This style is best for short items, and few of them. Mid-dots, commas or semicolons are available as separators (use semicolons or mid-dots if any items contain their own commas). For example: * {{para|parameter_name|{{tlp|hlist |Foo |bar |baz}}}} → {{hlist |Foo |bar |baz}} * {{para|parameter_name|{{tlp|cslist |Foo |bar |baz}}}} → {{cslist |Foo |bar |baz}} * {{para|parameter_name|{{tlp|cslist |Foo, fee |bar, bor |baz, biz |semi=true}}}} → {{cslist |Foo, fee |bar, bor |baz, biz |semi=true}} Horizontal list example with {{tlx|hlist|Item one|item two|item three}}: {{hlist|Item one|item two|item three}} '''Vertical''' templates are {{tlx|plainlist}} and {{tlx|unbulleted list}} (vertical), use [[Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Lists#Unbulleted lists|unbulleted, non-indented lists]] for clean display in infoboxes. Entries may be all [[sentence case]], or all lowercase (aside from proper names) after the first. This style is best for long items, and longer lists. For long lists of information that may not be of immediate interest but retained for reference, the {{tlx|collapsible list}} template can be used; this is not a universally accessible option, so should not be used for key information. ''[[Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Lists#Line breaks|Do not use {{tag|br|s}} markup]]'' to create fake lists, as in: {{!mxt|Item one
item two
item three}}. The HTML markup produced by this template includes an [[hCalendar|hCalendar microformat]], which makes the event details [[parsing|parsable]] by computers, either acting automatically to catalogue article across Wikipedia, or via a browser tool operated by a person, to (for example) add the subject to a calendar or diary application. Within the hCalendar is a [[Geo (microformat)|Geo microformat]], which additionally makes the [[geographic coordinate system|coordinates]] (latitude & longitude) parsable, so that they can be, say, looked up on a map, or downloaded to a [[Global Positioning System|GPS]] unit. For more information about the use of [[microformat]]s on Wikipedia, please see [[Wikipedia:WikiProject Microformats|the microformat project]]. Dates will only be included if you use {{tl|Start date}} or {{tl|End date}} (use the former for single dates, [[Wikipedia:WikiProject Microformats/dates|but do not use any of these if the date is before 1583 CE]]). {{tl|End date}} requires that a time be specified, but display of this time may be suppressed by adding {{para|nodate|yes}} to the end. To include a URL, use {{tl|URL}}. hCalendar uses HTML classes including: {{Flatlist|indent=1| *attendee *dtend *dtstart *location *summary *url *vevent }} Geo is produced by calling {{tl|coord}}, and uses HTML classes: {{Flatlist|indent=1| *geo *latitude *longitude }} '''Please do not rename or remove these classes nor collapse nested elements which use them.'''
Also, when giving coordinates, please don't be [[wikipedia:WikiProject Geographical coordinates#Precision|overly precise]]. {{#ifeq:{{SUBPAGENAME}}|doc | |{{#ifeq:{{SUBPAGENAME}}|sandbox | |[[Category:Templates generating hCalendars and Geo|{{PAGENAME}}]]}} }} [[Category:Microformat (uF) message templates]]

', y = ' .. y) local parent = frame:getParent() if parent then mw.log('Parent is ' .. parent:getTitle()) end mw.logObject(args, 'args') if currentTitle.namespace == 0 then local key = currentTitle.prefixedText builder:wikitext('[[Category:Location maps with marks outside map and outside parameter not set|' .. key .. ' ]]') end end local mark = args.mark or map('mark') if mark == '' then mark = 'Red pog.svg' end local marksize = tonumber(args.marksize) or tonumber(map('marksize')) or 8 local imageDiv = markImageDiv(mark, marksize, args.label or mw.title.getCurrentTitle().text, args.link or '', args.alt, args[2]) local labelDiv if args.label and args.position ~= 'none' then labelDiv = markLabelDiv(args.label, args.label_size or 91, args.label_width or 6, args.position, args.background, x, marksize) end return builder:node(markOuterDiv(x, y, imageDiv, labelDiv)) end local function switcherSeparate(s) if s == nil then return {} end local retval = {} for i in string.gmatch(s .. '#', '([^#]*)#') do i = mw.text.trim(i) retval[#retval + 1] = (i ~= '' and i) end return retval end function p.main(frame, args, map) local caption_list = {} if not args then args = getArgs(frame, {wrappers = 'Template:Location map', valueFunc = p.valueFunc}) end if args.useWikidata == nil then args.useWikidata = true end if not map then if args[1] then map = {} for mapname in string.gmatch(args[1], '[^#]+') do map[#map + 1] = p.getMapParams(mw.ustring.gsub(mapname, '^%s*(.-)%s*$', '%1'), frame) end if args['caption'] then if args['caption'] == "" then while #caption_list < #map do caption_list[#caption_list + 1] = args['caption'] end else for caption in mw.text.gsplit(args['caption'], '##', true) do caption_list[#caption_list + 1] = caption end end end if #map == 1 then map = map[1] end else map = p.getMapParams('World', frame) end end if type(map) == 'table' then local altmaps = switcherSeparate(args.AlternativeMap) if #altmaps > #map then error(string.format('%d AlternativeMaps were provided, but only %d maps were provided', #altmaps, #map)) end local overlays = switcherSeparate(args.overlay_image) if #overlays > #map then error(string.format('%d overlay_images were provided, but only %d maps were provided', #overlays, #map)) end if #caption_list > #map then error(string.format('%d captions were provided, but only %d maps were provided', #caption_list, #map)) end local outputs = {} args.autoSwitcherLabel = true for k,v in ipairs(map) do args.AlternativeMap = altmaps[k] args.overlay_image = overlays[k] args.caption = caption_list[k] outputs[k] = p.main(frame, args, v) end return '
' .. table.concat(outputs) .. '
' else return p.top(frame, args, map) .. tostring( p.mark(frame, args, map) ) .. p.bottom(frame, args, map) end end return p

==Usage== {{hatnote|Note: This template is for use on articles about '''individual people'''. For the infobox for use on articles about offices/positions, see [[Template:Infobox official post]].}} Paste the code for the relevant office and then add the [[#Personal data|personal data]] to the bottom. There are no required fields and some fields will not appear when others are in use. For instructions on how to implement multiple terms, see [[Template:Infobox officeholder/example#Multiple terms|this page]]. For advice on alt text, see ''[[Wikipedia:Alternative text for images]]''. The parameter {{para|order}} is used in conjunction with {{para|office}} to state that the officeholder is the ''n''th holder of the office, for example "42nd President of the United States". This should only be used when there is a well-established use of such numbering in reliable sources. Do not add numbers simply based on a Wikipedia list of holders of the office, because (1) the list may not be accurate and (2) even with a definite list, different numbering systems could be applied (as to how various categories of "irregular" officeholders should be counted, and as to the counting of those serving for multiple non-consecutive periods) making the numbers arbitrary; and even where such issues are not yet present, they are bound to be in the future, making this unsustainable. Per [[WP:SEAOFBLUE]], it is not recommended to wikilink {{para|order}} to a list of officeholders, even if such a list exists. If {{para|order}} is not specified, the value of {{para|office}} can be [[Help:Link#Wikilinks|wikilinked]] in the usual way, for example, "[[Ministry of Defence (Singapore)|Minister for Defence]]". However, if {{para|order}} is specified together with {{para|office}}, the value of {{para|office}} is automatically linked to a Wikipedia article of the same name, whether such an article exists or not. Wikilinking cannot be used to redirect the link elsewhere, but a [[Wikipedia:Piped link|piped link]] can be created like this: "Ministry of Defence (Singapore){{!}}Minister for Defence" (note that the double square brackets have been omitted). When both a start and an end term are given, you can instead specify the complete term using the parameters {{para|term}}, {{para|term2}}, etc. This can be helpful for complicated terms that cannot be given as simple starting or ending dates, or if you prefer something other than the default term separator (an en dash, with spaces around it if the start or end is not a simple integer date). Where a politician was redistricted into a new district, you can use {{para|prior_term}} to indicate which district(s) they were in before. This saves space in the infobox by not generating a completely new office each time redistricting happens. If you do this, it is recommended that you list the person who preceded the subject when the subject first took office and the person who succeeded the subject when the subject last left office. Where the use of "same district number" is used for determining "predecessor" and "successor" in any office, but where the area is so altered as to make such a "predecessor" or "successor" of little or no biographical value, the word "redistricted" should be used rather than using names of officeholders whose connection is accidental by virtue of district number, but unrelated to any election contests between officeholders. Please do not re-purpose any fields to add decorative images, icons or flags. Template:Infobox viceroy styles or the like can be used for this. [[WP:INFOBOXFLAG]] applies here. Per consensus in [[Wikipedia:Village pump (proposals)/Archive 175#RfC: Interim use of successor in Infobox officeholder|this RfC]], the infobox for an incumbent officeholder should not mention an [[-elect|elected or designated]] successor, or the end date of the term, until the successor takes office. ===General office=== {{For|examples of this code in use|Template:Infobox other templates == The ''module'' parameters (module, module2, ... module5) may used to embed other templates into this infobox (see [[Wikipedia:Infobox modules]]). {{Infobox officeholder | name = | | module = {{Infobox football biography | embed = yes | }} }} == Embedding within a different infobox == Many officeholders are known for more than just their appointments (e.g., [[Clint Eastwood]]), and hence it may be desirable to merge this infobox with another one, like {{tl|Infobox person}}. By adding {{para|embed|yes}} to the first line of the infobox code, one can embed this infobox into another, creating the illusion of one continuous infobox. Though the process is a little complicated, it is possible to insert this infobox into most if not all other infoboxes. For {{tl|Infobox person}}, this infobox is passed as a "module" using the {{para|module}} syntax. {{Infobox person | name = John Infobox | image = Example.jpg | caption = John Infobox in 2005 | birth_name = John Officeholder Person Infobox | birth_date = {{Birth date|1950|5|25}} | birth_place = Template City | death_date = {{Death date and age|2010|10|22|1950|5|25}} | occupation = Actor | years_active = 1970–1990 | module = {{Infobox officeholder | embed = yes | office = Mayor of Wikipedia | term_start = 1994 | term_end = 1998 }} | website = {{URL|example.com}} }} ==Microformat== ==Usage== {{hatnote|Note: This template is for use on articles about '''individual people'''. For the infobox for use on articles about offices/positions, see [[Template:Infobox official post]].}} Paste the code for the relevant office and then add the [[#Personal data|personal data]] to the bottom. There are no required fields and some fields will not appear when others are in use. For instructions on how to implement multiple terms, see [[Template:Infobox officeholder/example#Multiple terms|this page]]. For advice on alt text, see ''[[Wikipedia:Alternative text for images]]''. The parameter {{para|order}} is used in conjunction with {{para|office}} to state that the officeholder is the ''n''th holder of the office, for example "42nd President of the United States". This should only be used when there is a well-established use of such numbering in reliable sources. Do not add numbers simply based on a Wikipedia list of holders of the office, because (1) the list may not be accurate and (2) even with a definite list, different numbering systems could be applied (as to how various categories of "irregular" officeholders should be counted, and as to the counting of those serving for multiple non-consecutive periods) making the numbers arbitrary; and even where such issues are not yet present, they are bound to be in the future, making this unsustainable. Per [[WP:SEAOFBLUE]], it is not recommended to wikilink {{para|order}} to a list of officeholders, even if such a list exists. If {{para|order}} is not specified, the value of {{para|office}} can be [[Help:Link#Wikilinks|wikilinked]] in the usual way, for example, "[[Ministry of Defence (Singapore)|Minister for Defence]]". However, if {{para|order}} is specified together with {{para|office}}, the value of {{para|office}} is automatically linked to a Wikipedia article of the same name, whether such an article exists or not. Wikilinking cannot be used to redirect the link elsewhere, but a [[Wikipedia:Piped link|piped link]] can be created like this: "Ministry of Defence (Singapore){{!}}Minister for Defence" (note that the double square brackets have been omitted). When both a start and an end term are given, you can instead specify the complete term using the parameters {{para|term}}, {{para|term2}}, etc. This can be helpful for complicated terms that cannot be given as simple starting or ending dates, or if you prefer something other than the default term separator (an en dash, with spaces around it if the start or end is not a simple integer date). Where a politician was redistricted into a new district, you can use {{para|prior_term}} to indicate which district(s) they were in before. This saves space in the infobox by not generating a completely new office each time redistricting happens. If you do this, it is recommended that you list the person who preceded the subject when the subject first took office and the person who succeeded the subject when the subject last left office. Where the use of "same district number" is used for determining "predecessor" and "successor" in any office, but where the area is so altered as to make such a "predecessor" or "successor" of little or no biographical value, the word "redistricted" should be used rather than using names of officeholders whose connection is accidental by virtue of district number, but unrelated to any election contests between officeholders. Please do not re-purpose any fields to add decorative images, icons or flags. Template:Infobox viceroy styles or the like can be used for this. [[WP:INFOBOXFLAG]] applies here. Per consensus in [[Wikipedia:Village pump (proposals)/Archive 175#RfC: Interim use of successor in Infobox officeholder|this RfC]], the infobox for an incumbent officeholder should not mention an [[-elect|elected or designated]] successor, or the end date of the term, until the successor takes office. ===General office=== {{For|examples of this code in use|Template:Infobox other templates == The ''module'' parameters (module, module2, ... module5) may used to embed other templates into this infobox (see [[Wikipedia:Infobox modules]]). {{Infobox officeholder | name = | | module = {{Infobox football biography | embed = yes | }} }} == Embedding within a different infobox == Many officeholders are known for more than just their appointments (e.g., [[Clint Eastwood]]), and hence it may be desirable to merge this infobox with another one, like {{tl|Infobox person}}. By adding {{para|embed|yes}} to the first line of the infobox code, one can embed this infobox into another, creating the illusion of one continuous infobox. Though the process is a little complicated, it is possible to insert this infobox into most if not all other infoboxes. For {{tl|Infobox person}}, this infobox is passed as a "module" using the {{para|module}} syntax. {{Infobox person | name = John Infobox | image = Example.jpg | caption = John Infobox in 2005 | birth_name = John Officeholder Person Infobox | birth_date = {{Birth date|1950|5|25}} | birth_place = Template City | death_date = {{Death date and age|2010|10|22|1950|5|25}} | occupation = Actor | --[[ SDcat Module to check whether local short description matches that on Wikidata --]]
local p = {}
------------------------------------------------------------------------------- --[[ setCat has the qid of a Wikidata entity passed as |qid= (it defaults to the associated qid of the current article if omitted) and the local short description passed as |sd= It returns a category if there is an associated Wikidata entity. It returns one of the following tracking categories, as appropriate: * Category:Short description matches Wikidata (case-insensitive) * Category:Short description is different from Wikidata * Category:Short description with empty Wikidata description For testing purposes, a link prefix |lp= may be set to ":" to make the categories visible. --]]
-- function exported for use in other modules -- (local short description, Wikidata entity-ID, link prefix) p._setCat = function(sdesc, itemID, lp) if not mw.wikibase then return nil end if itemID == "" then itemID = nil end -- Wikidata description field local wdesc = (mw.wikibase.getDescription(itemID) or ""):lower() if wdesc == "" then return "[[" .. lp .. "Category:Short description with empty Wikidata description]]" elseif wdesc == sdesc then return "[[" .. lp .. "Category:Short description matches Wikidata]]" else return "[[" .. lp .. "Category:Short description is different from Wikidata]]" end end
-- function exported for call from #invoke p.setCat = function(frame) local args if frame.args.sd then args = frame.args else args = frame:getParent().args end -- local short description local sdesc = mw.text.trim(args.sd or ""):lower() -- Wikidata entity-ID local itemID = mw.text.trim(args.qid or "") -- link prefix, strip quotes local lp = mw.text.trim(args.lp or ""):gsub('"', '') return p._setCat(sdesc, itemID, lp) end
return p

'''Astoria''' is a [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stratocracy Stratocracy] located on the continent of [[Viridia]] and was formed in 1834 from the ashes of the [[Republic of Astoria]].
== Government ==
=== Political Sphere === Astoria is governed by a Stratocracy, where military rule dominates the political landscape. The country's military holds the highest authority and exercises direct control over governance and decision-making processes. The Astorian military, known as the Astorian Armed Forces (AAF) or Vanguard Order, plays a central role in the nation's administration and policy formulation. The highest-ranking military officials form the ruling council, collectively known as the Military Council, which acts as the de facto governing body. The Military Council determines national policies, makes legislative decisions, and oversees the implementation of laws and regulations. The military's influence extends to all areas of governance, including the economy, education, and social affairs. Military leaders are appointed to key administrative positions and are responsible for managing government departments, public services, and infrastructure development. Political power is concentrated within the military hierarchy, and civilian representation is limited. However, a Civilian Advisory Council may be established to provide limited input and advice to the Military Council on matters related to civilian life and public welfare. While the Stratocracy emphasizes military discipline and efficiency, it also aims to maintain stability and security within the country. The military's primary focus is on protecting Astoria's borders, safeguarding national interests, and responding to internal and external threats. Civil liberties and democratic processes may be restricted under the Stratocracy. Freedom of speech and assembly may be curtailed, and political opposition is suppressed to maintain order and cohesion within society. The military's role extends to enforcing strict social and cultural norms, maintaining social control, and ensuring loyalty to the state. While Astoria's political system is dominated by military leadership, efforts may be made to provide essential services, education, and welfare to citizens. The military may invest in infrastructure development, prioritize national security, and maintain law and order. Astoria's foreign policy may focus on maintaining a strong defense posture, establishing regional alliances, and protecting national interests. The Stratocracy may emphasize military readiness and cooperation with other nations in matters of security and defense.
=== Economic Sphere === Astoria's mixed-market economy is driven by a balance between private enterprise and government involvement. The country encourages entrepreneurship, innovation, and competition, while also recognizing the importance of strategic planning and public welfare. The private sector in Astoria plays a vital role in driving economic growth and employment. It encompasses a wide range of industries, including manufacturing, services, technology, and agriculture. Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) form the backbone of the economy, fostering a vibrant entrepreneurial culture and providing significant employment opportunities. Astoria's government actively participates in shaping economic policies to ensure fair competition, promote social welfare, and foster sustainable development. It establishes regulations and safeguards to prevent market monopolies, protect consumer rights, and maintain environmental standards. Strategic sectors, such as energy, infrastructure, and defense, may see significant government intervention to ensure long-term stability and security. The government may invest in critical infrastructure projects, support research and development initiatives, and provide incentives for industries of national importance. Astoria promotes international trade and foreign investments, striving to create a favorable business environment. The country's strategic location, skilled workforce, and natural resources attract foreign companies and facilitate trade partnerships. Astoria also seeks to diversify its export base, promoting high-value-added products and services. The government emphasizes education and human capital development to meet the demands of a dynamic economy. Investment in education and vocational training programs equips the workforce with the necessary skills to adapt to changing industry trends and technological advancements. Astoria recognizes the importance of social welfare and endeavors to reduce income inequality. The government implements social safety nets, healthcare programs, and initiatives to support vulnerable populations, ensuring a basic standard of living for all citizens. Environmental sustainability is a priority in Astoria's economic sphere. The country promotes green initiatives, encourages renewable energy development, and implements policies to mitigate climate change impacts, however the Astorian Economy has been slow to move towards this green initiative. Although, Astoria's commitment to environmental stewardship ensures the long-term health of its natural resources and supports eco-friendly industries. Overall, Astoria's mixed-market economy combines private enterprise with government intervention to foster economic growth, social welfare, and sustainability. It encourages entrepreneurship, innovation, and international trade while prioritizing strategic sectors, social equity, and environmental protection.
=== Military Sphere === Astoria's military sphere is known as the Vanguard Order, representing a distinctive blend of traditional warrior culture and modern strategic capabilities. The Vanguard Order is renowned for its elite combat units, exceptional training, and a deep sense of honor and loyalty. The military's structure combines ancient martial traditions with cutting-edge technology and tactics. The Vanguard Order upholds the principles of chivalry, discipline, and bravery, emphasizing the code of conduct that guides its members both on and off the battlefield. Astoria's military excels in special operations and unconventional warfare, with specialized units trained for covert missions, intelligence gathering, and counterterrorism. The Vanguard Order's expertise extends to cyber warfare, ensuring the nation's digital security and defending against emerging threats in the virtual realm. Astoria's military fosters innovation and creativity, encouraging its personnel to think outside the box and adapt to changing circumstances. The Vanguard Order supports research and development initiatives, collaborating with Academia and private sector partners to drive technological advancements and maintain a competitive edge. The military sphere of Astoria also places a strong emphasis on it's Sphere of Influence. The Vanguard Order actively participates in neighboring countries matters, willingly or forcefully. Astoria's military embraces diversity and inclusivity, welcoming individuals from all backgrounds and identities. The Vanguard Order promotes equal opportunities for all, ensuring that talent and merit are the guiding factors in recruitment and advancement. Astoria's military symbolizes courage, resilience, and a commitment to protect the nation's values and interests. The Vanguard Order's disciplined warriors, guided by a code of honor and equipped with cutting-edge technology, stand as a formidable force dedicated to defending Astoria and expanding Astoria's Influence Globally.

'''Astoria''' is a [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stratocracy Stratocracy] located on the continent of [[Viridia]]. Founded in 1834 from the remnants of the [[Republic of Astoria]], it has evolved into a powerful military state with significant regional influence.
== History == Astoria emerged in 1834 following the collapse of the Republic of Astoria. The transition to a stratocratic government marked a significant shift in the nation's political and social structure, establishing the foundation for its current military-dominated system.
== Government and Politics == === Political Structure === Astoria operates as a stratocracy, with the military serving as the primary governing body. The Astorian Armed Forces (AAF), also known as the Vanguard Order, maintains supreme authority over all aspects of governance.
==== Military Council ==== The Military Council serves as the de facto governing body of Astoria. Composed of the highest-ranking military officials, it holds responsibility for national policy formulation and oversees all legislative decisions and law implementation. This council represents the pinnacle of military authority in the nation's governance structure.
==== Civilian Advisory Council ==== The Civilian Advisory Council provides limited civilian input to the Military Council, focusing primarily on matters of civilian life and public welfare. While it operates under military oversight, it serves as a crucial bridge between the military leadership and the civilian population, ensuring that civilian concerns are at least considered in the decision-making process.
=== Political Climate === The political climate in Astoria is characterized by complete military dominance in all aspects of governance. Civil liberties and democratic processes are significantly restricted, with a strong emphasis placed on stability and national security. Political opposition is limited, and the government strictly enforces social and cultural norms to maintain order and cohesion within society.
== Economy == === Economic System === Astoria maintains a mixed-market economy that balances private enterprise with strategic government intervention. This system allows for both economic freedom and necessary government oversight in critical sectors.
=== Key Economic Features === The private sector plays a vital role in Astoria's economy, with strong presence in manufacturing, services, technology, and agriculture. The government maintains regulatory control over strategic sectors such as energy, infrastructure, and defense. Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) receive significant support, while the nation actively promotes international trade and foreign investment. A strong focus on human capital development and education ensures a skilled workforce capable of meeting the demands of a modern economy.
=== Economic Priorities === Astoria's economic priorities center around comprehensive infrastructure development and robust research and development initiatives. The government implements various social welfare programs while working to reduce income inequality. Environmental sustainability remains a stated goal, though implementation has been slow. These priorities reflect the nation's commitment to both economic growth and social welfare.
== Military == === Vanguard Order === The Vanguard Order represents Astoria's military might, combining traditional warrior culture with modern strategic capabilities. This elite force serves as both the nation's military arm and its governing body.
=== Military Characteristics === The Vanguard Order is renowned for its elite combat units and specialized training programs. It maintains a strong emphasis on honor and loyalty, integrating ancient martial traditions with modern technology. The military excels in special operations and unconventional warfare, with advanced capabilities in cyber warfare. This combination of traditional values and modern capabilities makes the Vanguard Order a formidable military force.
=== Military Influence === The Vanguard Order actively participates in regional affairs, with a strong emphasis on expanding Astoria's sphere of influence. It maintains an unwavering commitment to national defense and security while promoting diversity and merit-based advancement within its ranks. The military places significant focus on technological innovation and adaptation, ensuring it remains at the forefront of military capabilities.
== Society and Culture == === Demographics === Astoria's population is predominantly Astorian, making up 99.9% of the total population. The official language is Astorian, and Warka serves as the state religion. This demographic homogeneity contributes to the nation's strong cultural identity.
=== Social Structure === Astoria's social structure is heavily influenced by its military hierarchy. The society places great emphasis on discipline and national loyalty, with military values deeply integrated into civilian life. This integration fosters a strong sense of national unity and cohesion, creating a society that values order, duty, and service to the state.

The democratic republic that preceded the current government faced significant challenges in maintaining order and stability. The military's centralized control and disciplined organizational structure proved instrumental in driving rapid industrialization. The military's direct involvement in administration facilitated the swift implementation of industrial projects, significantly enhancing Astoria's industrial capabilities and economic strength.

Growing civil unrest and demands for democratic representation following various conflicts led to the introduction of the Civil Liberties Act of 1928. = Astoria =
The '''Astoria''' is a [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stratocracy Stratocracy] located on the continent of [[Viridia]]. Founded in 1834 from the remnants of the [[Republic of Astoria]], it has evolved into a powerful military state with significant regional influence. Known for its formidable military capabilities and strict hierarchical structure, Astoria maintains a unique position as one of the world's most powerful military states.
= History =
== Pre-Stratocracy Era (1800-1822) == The Republic of Astoria, established in the early 19th century, was characterized by a fragile democratic system struggling to maintain stability in a region marked by political turmoil. The republic faced numerous challenges, including economic instability, social unrest, and external pressures from neighboring states. The civilian government's inability to effectively address these issues created a power vacuum that the military would eventually fill.
== The Rise of the Stratocracy (1822-1834) == The foundation of modern Astoria began with a period of internal strife and civil unrest in the early 19th century. The democratic republic that preceded the current government faced significant challenges in maintaining order and stability. In 1834, under the leadership of Lord Commander Mustafa Kaynarca, the Astorian Armed Forces staged a decisive coup to restore order. This marked the beginning of the Stratocracy, with the military assuming complete control of governance while promising security and stability to the citizens.
The transition to military rule was not without resistance, but the Astorian Armed Forces, under Kaynarca's leadership, successfully consolidated power through a combination of strategic alliances and decisive action. The new military government established the foundations of what would become the Vanguard Order, implementing strict discipline and hierarchical structures that would define Astoria's governance for centuries to come.
== Consolidation Period (1834-1892) == The decades following the establishment of the Stratocracy were marked by significant political and social transformation. The military government implemented sweeping reforms across all sectors of society, establishing the Military Council as the supreme governing body and creating the Civilian Advisory Council to maintain a connection with the civilian population.
This period saw the development of Astoria's unique military culture, with the establishment of military academies and training institutions that would produce generations of disciplined officers. The government also began implementing its vision of a society where military values and discipline permeated all aspects of life, from education to industry.
== Industrial Development (1892-1905) == The late 19th century witnessed a remarkable transformation in Astoria's economic landscape. The military's centralized control and disciplined organizational structure proved instrumental in driving rapid industrialization. This period, known as the Astorian Industrial Surge, saw unprecedented infrastructural development and efficient resource allocation.
The military's direct involvement in administration facilitated the swift implementation of industrial projects, significantly enhancing Astoria's industrial capabilities and economic strength. Factories, railways, and modern infrastructure were constructed at an unprecedented pace, transforming Astoria from an agricultural society into an industrial power. The military's ability to mobilize resources and manpower proved crucial in this transformation, demonstrating the effectiveness of the Stratocratic system in driving economic development.
== Political Evolution (1905-1928) == The early 20th century brought new challenges to Astoria's military rule. The rapid industrialization and urbanization of the previous decades had created a more complex society with new demands and expectations. Growing civil unrest and demands for democratic representation following various conflicts led to the introduction of the Civil Liberties Act of 1928.
While maintaining its dominant role in governance, the military introduced limited civilian representation and participation through this act. This marked a significant, though controlled, step toward political liberalization while preserving the core principles of the Stratocracy. The act established the framework for civilian participation in governance while ensuring that ultimate authority remained with the military leadership.
== Military Modernization (1928-1990) == The mid-20th century saw significant developments in Astoria's military capabilities and international standing. The Vanguard Order, as the military came to be known, underwent extensive modernization and reorganization. New military doctrines were developed, incorporating both traditional warrior values and modern strategic thinking.
This period also saw the expansion of Astoria's military-industrial complex, with significant investments in research and development of new technologies. The military's role in society became even more entrenched, with military values and discipline becoming central to Astorian identity. The Vanguard Order's influence extended beyond traditional military matters, playing a crucial role in education, industry, and cultural development.
== Modern Era (1990-Present) == The modern era of Astoria has been defined by its military prowess and regional influence. During the Avant World War (1990-1994), Astoria maintained a position of neutrality, though it showed support for Solara as a gesture of goodwill. This period also saw the consolidation of Astoria's military capabilities and the refinement of its governance structure.
Under the leadership of Lord Commander Ruslan Cengiz, Astoria has continued to evolve while maintaining its core principles of military governance. The nation has successfully balanced its traditional military values with the demands of a modern, technologically advanced society. The Vanguard Order has adapted to new challenges, incorporating cyber warfare capabilities and modern military technologies while preserving its traditional warrior culture.
The nation's military history has been marked by both triumphs and challenges, with various conflicts shaping its development and international standing. These experiences have contributed to the evolution of Astoria's military doctrine and its approach to regional affairs. The Vanguard Order, as the modern incarnation of the Astorian military, continues to play a central role in both national defense and governance.
= Government and politics =
== Political Structure == Astoria operates as a stratocracy, with the military serving as the primary governing body. The Astorian Armed Forces (AAF), also known as the Vanguard Order, maintains supreme authority over all aspects of governance. The Military Council serves as the de facto governing body of Astoria, composed of the highest-ranking military officials who hold responsibility for national policy formulation and oversee all legislative decisions and law implementation.
The Civilian Advisory Council provides limited civilian input to the Military Council, focusing primarily on matters of civilian life and public welfare. While it operates under military oversight, it serves as a crucial bridge between the military leadership and the civilian population, ensuring that civilian concerns are at least considered in the decision-making process.
== Political Climate == The political climate in Astoria is characterized by complete military dominance in all aspects of governance. Civil liberties and democratic processes are significantly restricted, with a strong emphasis placed on stability and national security. Political opposition is limited, and the government strictly enforces social and cultural norms to maintain order and cohesion within society.
== Economy == Astoria maintains a mixed-market economy that balances private enterprise with strategic government intervention. The private sector plays a vital role in Astoria's economy, with strong presence in manufacturing, services, technology, and agriculture. The government maintains regulatory control over strategic sectors such as energy, infrastructure, and defense.
Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) receive significant support, while the nation actively promotes international trade and foreign investment. A strong focus on human capital development and education ensures a skilled workforce capable of meeting the demands of a modern economy.
Astoria's economic priorities center around comprehensive infrastructure development and robust research and development initiatives. Known for its formidable military capabilities and strict hierarchical structure, Astoria maintains a unique position as one of the world's most powerful military states.
= History =
== Early History (1800-1834) == The Republic of Astoria emerged in the early 19th century as a fragile democracy in a region marked by political instability. The civilian government struggled to maintain order amidst growing social unrest and economic challenges. The military gradually gained influence as the only institution capable of maintaining stability, particularly after several border conflicts with neighboring states. By the 1820s, the military had become a dominant force in Astorian politics, setting the stage for a fundamental transformation of the nation's political system.
== The Rise of the Stratocracy (1834-1892) == In 1834, following years of political turmoil and government paralysis, Lord Commander Mustafa Kaynarca led the Astorian Armed Forces in a decisive coup. The military's takeover marked the beginning of the Stratocracy, with the military assuming complete control of governance. The new government established the Military Council as the supreme governing body and began implementing its vision of a society organized along military lines.
This period saw the establishment of the Vanguard Order and the systematic reorganization of society. The military government implemented sweeping reforms across all sectors, from education to industry. Resistance to the new regime was met with swift action, while the military's intelligence services were expanded to monitor potential threats. The foundations of modern Astoria were laid during these decades, with military values becoming central to Astorian identity.
The late 19th century witnessed a remarkable transformation in Astoria's capabilities. The military's centralized control proved instrumental in driving rapid industrialization, known as the Astorian Industrial Surge. Infrastructure, manufacturing, and technology developed at an unprecedented pace, transforming Astoria from an agricultural society into an industrial power. This period also saw significant advancements in military technology and doctrine, with the Vanguard Order undergoing extensive modernization and incorporating new weapons systems and tactics.
== Modernization and Reform (1892-1990) == The early 20th century brought new challenges to Astoria's military rule. Growing civil unrest and demands for democratic representation led to the introduction of the Civil Liberties Act of 1928. While maintaining its dominant role in governance, the military introduced limited civilian representation through the Civilian Advisory Council. This marked a significant, though controlled, step toward political liberalization while preserving the core principles of the Stratocracy.
The mid-20th century saw further developments in Astoria's military capabilities and international standing. The Vanguard Order underwent extensive modernization and reorganization, developing new military doctrines that combined traditional warrior values with modern strategic thinking. The military's role in society became even more entrenched, with military values and discipline becoming central to Astorian identity.
== Modern Era (1990-Present) == The modern era of Astoria has been defined by its military prowess and regional influence. During the Avant World War (1990-1994), Astoria maintained a position of neutrality, though it showed support for Solara as a gesture of goodwill. This period saw the consolidation of Astoria's military capabilities and the refinement of its governance structure.
Under the leadership of Lord Commander Ruslan Cengiz, Astoria has continued to evolve while maintaining its core principles of military governance. The nation has successfully balanced its traditional military values with the demands of a modern, technologically advanced society. The Vanguard Order has adapted to new challenges, incorporating cyber warfare capabilities and modern military technologies while preserving its traditional warrior culture.
= Government and politics =
== Political Structure == Astoria operates as a stratocracy, with the military serving as the primary governing body. The Astorian Armed Forces (AAF), also known as the Vanguard Order, maintains supreme authority over all aspects of governance. The Military Council serves as the de facto governing body of Astoria, composed of the highest-ranking military officials who hold responsibility for national policy formulation and oversee all legislative decisions and law implementation.
The Civilian Advisory Council provides limited civilian input to the Military Council, focusing primarily on matters of civilian life and public welfare. While it operates under military oversight, it serves as a crucial bridge between the military leadership and the civilian population, ensuring that civilian concerns are at least considered in the decision-making process.
== Political Climate == The political climate in Astoria is characterized by complete military dominance in all aspects of governance. Civil liberties and democratic processes are significantly restricted, with a strong emphasis placed on stability and national security. Political opposition is limited, and the government strictly enforces social and cultural norms to maintain order and cohesion within society.
== Economy == Astoria maintains a mixed-market economy that balances private enterprise with strategic government intervention. The private sector plays a vital role in Astoria's economy, with strong presence in manufacturing, services, technology, and agriculture. The government maintains regulatory control over strategic sectors such as energy, infrastructure, and defense.
Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) receive significant support, while the nation actively promotes international trade and foreign investment. A strong focus on human capital development and education ensures a skilled workforce capable of meeting the demands of a modern economy.
Astoria's economic priorities center around comprehensive infrastructure development and robust research and development initiatives. The government implements various social welfare programs while working to reduce income inequality. Environmental sustainability remains a stated goal, though implementation has been slow.
== Military == [[File:AstoriaMilitary.jpg|thumb|'''Vanguard Order Forces on Parade''']]
The Vanguard Order represents Astoria's military might, combining traditional warrior culture with modern strategic capabilities. This elite force serves as both the nation's military arm and its governing body. The Vanguard Order is renowned for its elite combat units and specialized training programs, maintaining a strong emphasis on honor and loyalty while integrating ancient martial traditions with modern technology.
The military excels in special operations and unconventional warfare, with advanced capabilities in cyber warfare. This combination of traditional values and modern capabilities makes the Vanguard Order a formidable military force. The Vanguard Order actively participates in regional affairs, with a strong emphasis on expanding Astoria's sphere of influence. It maintains an unwavering commitment to national defense and security while promoting diversity and merit-based advancement within its ranks.
== Society and Culture == Astoria's population is predominantly Astorian, making up 99.9% of the total population. The official language is Astorian, and Warka serves as the state religion. This demographic homogeneity contributes to the nation's strong cultural identity.
Astoria's social structure is heavily influenced by its military hierarchy. The society places great emphasis on discipline and national loyalty, with military values deeply integrated into civilian life. This integration fosters a strong sense of national unity and cohesion, creating a society that values order, duty, and service to the state.

== Early History (1700–1834) == The story of Astoria in the 18th and early 19th centuries is one of endurance, resistance, and the gradual reawakening of a national spirit under foreign domination. These Caliphates imposed a rigid order upon the Astorian lands, enforcing heavy taxation, conscription, and the suppression of local customs, language, and religious practices. Astorian communities were often subject to the authority of distant governors and religious officials, who sought to integrate the region into the broader imperial system and erase its distinct identity.
Yet, beneath the surface, Astorian culture endured. In the highland villages, forest enclaves, and remote valleys, traditions were preserved in secret—songs, rituals, and the old tongue passed down from generation to generation. Local chieftains, clandestine brotherhoods, and spiritual leaders became the stewards of a hidden national consciousness, quietly resisting the encroachment of foreign rule. Periodic revolts erupted throughout the 17th and early 18th centuries, each met with harsh reprisals but never fully extinguishing the hope of freedom.
The mid-1700s brought a dramatic shift. The Caliphates, weakened by internal strife, economic decline, and the growing ambitions of the Vesperan Empire in the eastern interior, found their grip on the Astorian territories slipping. Sensing opportunity, Astorian leaders—most notably the Kaynarca family of Bokevrek—began to unite the scattered resistance. Through a combination of guerrilla warfare, strategic alliances, and appeals to shared heritage, they rallied both peasants and dispossessed nobles to their cause.
As the Caliphate garrisons withdrew and imperial authority crumbled, the Kaynarca dynasty emerged as the architects of a new Astorian order. By the late 18th century, they had succeeded in expelling the last vestiges of foreign rule, uniting the city-states and rural communities under their banner. The monarchy they established was deeply shaped by the memory of occupation: it drew legitimacy from its role as liberator, and its institutions were infused with a sense of vigilance and national pride.
This era of liberation forged a resilient Astorian identity—one that remembered both the pain of subjugation and the triumph of self-determination. The legacy of Caliphate rule, and the shared experience of resistance, left enduring cultural and familial ties with the peoples of the east, foreshadowing future interactions with the lands that would become Volgastan. = History =
== Early History (1700–1834) == From the early 1600s through the mid-1700s, the territories that would become Astoria were under the control of a series of eastern caliphates, most notably the Arashiyun Caliphate and the Mamoonid Caliphate. These states, centered in what is now eastern Khalari and western Volgastan, extended their authority westward through military occupation, religious administration, and the appointment of provincial governors (beys and pashas) in Astorian lands.
The Arashiyun and Mamoonid caliphates imposed heavy taxation, conscription, and restrictions on local customs, seeking to integrate the region into their broader imperial system. Astorian communities, especially in the highlands and along the coast, maintained their language, traditions, and social structures in defiance of these policies. Secret gatherings, local religious leaders (imams and hodjas), and family networks played a key role in preserving Astorian identity.
Throughout the 17th and early 18th centuries, there were several notable uprisings against caliphal rule, including the Bokevrek Revolt (1724) and the Uluova Resistance (1741–1745). As the Arashiyun and Mamoonid caliphates weakened due to internal conflict and external pressures—including the expansion of the Vesperan Empire in the east—Astorian leaders, particularly the Kaynarca family of Bokevrek, began to organize a more coordinated resistance.

The monarchy's legitimacy was rooted in its role as the liberator of Astoria and the restorer of Astorian traditions. This period forged a strong sense of national identity, with enduring cultural and familial ties to the peoples of the east, especially those in the former caliphate territories that would later become Volgastan.

The '''Astoria''' is a [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stratocracy Stratocracy] located on the continent of [[Viridia]]. Founded in 1834 from the remnants of the [[Republic of Astoria]], it has evolved into a powerful military state with significant regional influence. Known for its formidable military capabilities and strict hierarchical structure, Astoria maintains a unique position as one of the world's most powerful military states.
= History =
== Early History (1700–1834) == From the early 1600s through the mid-1700s, the territories that would become Astoria were under the control of a series of eastern caliphates, most notably the Arashiyun Caliphate and the Mamoonid Caliphate. These states, centered in what is now eastern Khalari and western Volgastan, extended their authority westward through military occupation, religious administration, and the appointment of provincial governors (beys and pashas) in Astorian lands.
The Arashiyun and Mamoonid caliphates imposed heavy taxation, conscription, and restrictions on local customs, seeking to integrate the region into their broader imperial system. Astorian communities, especially in the highlands and along the coast, maintained their language, traditions, and social structures in defiance of these policies. Secret gatherings, local religious leaders (imams and hodjas), and family networks played a key role in preserving Astorian identity.
Throughout the 17th and early 18th centuries, there were several notable uprisings against caliphal rule, including the Bokevrek Revolt (1724) and the Uluova Resistance (1741–1745). These revolts were often suppressed, but they laid the groundwork for future unity. As the Arashiyun and Mamoonid caliphates weakened due to internal conflict and external pressures—including the expansion of the Vesperan Empire in the east—Astorian leaders, particularly the Kaynarca family of Bokevrek, began to organize a more coordinated resistance.
By the late 18th century, the Astorians launched a series of coordinated campaigns to expel the remaining caliphal forces. The Kaynarca dynasty, working with local beys and influential families, established a network of fortified villages and supply routes through the highlands. Guerrilla tactics, sabotage of supply lines, and targeted attacks on isolated garrisons gradually wore down the occupying armies. The decisive moment came during the Siege of Bokevrek (1787), when Astorian forces, supported by local militias and defected mercenaries, encircled and forced the surrender of the largest Arashiyun garrison in the region. This victory inspired a wave of uprisings across the countryside, leading to the rapid collapse of caliphal authority.
During this period, the Pesterans and Bakorians—neighboring peoples to the north and east—were also under occupation by the caliphates and engaged in their own resistance efforts. Like the Astorians, they faced heavy taxation, forced conscription, and suppression of their cultural practices. There were instances of cooperation between Astorian, Pesteran, and Bakorian resistance groups, including clandestine trade, intelligence sharing, and joint raids on caliphal outposts. These shared struggles fostered a sense of solidarity and occasional alliances, even as each group pursued its own path to liberation.
By the end of the 18th century, the last caliphal garrisons withdrew from Astoria. The Kaynarca dynasty established itself as the ruling house, uniting the region's city-states and rural communities. The monarchy's legitimacy was rooted in its role as the liberator of Astoria and the restorer of Astorian traditions. This period forged a strong sense of national identity, with enduring cultural and familial ties to the peoples of the east, especially those in the former caliphate territories that would later become Volgastan.
