revision.text:
{{Lua|Module:Documentation}} This is the {{tlf|Documentation}} template, used on almost every template page to contain that template's documented instructions and information. For detailed instructions on how and when to use this template, see [[w:Wikipedia:Template documentation]]. This template displays a green documentation box like you are seeing now and automatically loads the content from a /doc subpage. It can also load the content from other places if instructed to. This template is intended for documenting templates and other pages that are [[w:Wikipedia:Transclusion|transcluded]] onto other pages. It can be used in the [[w:Wikipedia:Template namespace|template namespace]] and most other [[w:Wikipedia:Namespace|namespace]]s. Use of this template allows templates to be [[w:Wikipedia:Protection policy|protected]] where necessary, while allowing anyone to edit the documentation and categories. ===Usage=== Normally this template is used without any parameters, placed at the bottom of the template or page being documented, within a {{tag|noinclude}} container: {{Documentation}} Then this template automatically loads the content from the /doc subpage of the template it is used on. This template can also load the content from any other page. Like this: {{Documentation |Template:Other page/doc}} Note that when loading the documentation from a page other than the local /doc page it becomes tricky to handle the categories. The content can also be fed directly as text. Like this: {{Documentation | content = (some documentation) }} When the {{para|content}} parameter is used, the doc box normally does not show the [edit] [purge] links in the top right corner. Note that if the /doc page exists, a link to it is still shown in the link box below the doc box. Parameter {{para|1}} and the {{para|content}} parameter can also be combined, like this: {{Documentation |1=Template:Any page/doc | content = {{Template:Any page/doc |parameters}} }} Then the pagename fed as parameter 1 is used for the [edit] [purge] links and for the /doc link in the link box below the doc box. But the '''content''' parameter is used for the content shown in the doc box. The above code means that the content is transcluded as {{tnull|Template:Any page/doc{{!}}parameters}}. In this example a parameter is also fed to the /doc page being loaded. === Shortcut === To automatically insert the [[w:Wikipedia:Noinclude|noinclude tags]], the template call and the guiding comment, use this [[w:WP:Substitution|substitution]] code:
:{{subst:doc-code}} ===Best practice=== The code should be added at the bottom of the template code, with no space before {{Tag|noinclude|o}} (which would cause extra space on pages where the template is used). Categories that apply to the template itself should be added to the bottom of the /doc subpage, inside {{Tag|includeonly}} tags. Interwiki links that apply to the template should be listed at [[d:|Wikidata]] (more at [[w:Wikipedia:Wikidata|wp:Wikidata]]). For more complex cases, see [[w:Wikipedia:Template documentation#Categories and interwiki links]]. If the documentation page contains {{tag|includeonly|o}} or {{tag|noinclude|o}} tags as part of the visible documentation text, replace the "<" with "<" or use [[Template:tag]]. ===Heading=== When in the Template namespace, this template shows this heading: :[[File:Test Template Info-Icon - Version (2).svg|32px|link=[[w:Wikipedia:Template documentation]]]] '''Template documentation''' In most other namespaces, such as "{{SITENAME}}:", it shows this heading: :'''Documentation''' But when on File (image) pages it shows this heading: :'''Summary''' The '''heading''' parameter can be used to set the heading to something else. Like this: :{{Documentation |heading=Infobox documentation}} If the '''heading''' parameter is empty but defined, no heading is shown and no [edit] [purge] links are shown. Like this: :{{Documentation |heading=}} The '''heading-style''' parameter can be fed optional [[w:Cascading Style Sheets|CSS]] values. Without quotation marks " " but with the ending semicolons ;. For example: :heading-style=font-size:150%;color:red; ===Link box=== Below the big doc box is a small link box that shows some meta-data about the documentation. The link box shows different things depending on what parameters are fed to this template, and in which namespace it is used. In some cases the link box is not shown at all. To hide the link box, add the parameter : {{para|link box|off}}. You can also insert customised text into the link box, by setting the {{para|link box}} parameter. For example: 
  |link box=This documentation is automatically generated by [[w:Template:Country showdata]]
===Automatic functions=== If the documentation page does not exist, the [create] link includes a [[mw:Manual:Creating pages with preloaded text|preload]] page so that clicking it will pre-fill the edit form with the basic documentation page format. Preload text is also used for the /sandbox and /testcases [create] links. When this template is on a protected template page it now automatically adds {{tl|pp-template}}, which shows the grey or red padlock in the top right corner. So no need to manually add {{tlf|pp-template}} to templates that use {{tl|Documentation}}. When this template is on a /sandbox subpage it automatically adds the {{tl|Template sandbox notice}}. ===Subject namespaces vs. talk namespaces=== Terminology: ''Subject namespaces'' are the opposite of ''talk namespaces''. For instance "Template:" is the subject space of "Template talk:". This template is usually placed in a subject namespace, within {{tag|noinclude|o}} tags. But in some cases this template needs to be on the talk page: * In the Mediawiki namespace, since {{tag|noinclude|o}} often does not work in system messages, and since the Mediawiki namespace needs to be kept clean for performance reasons. When placed on talk pages, this template usually is placed near the top of the page and without {{tag|noinclude}} tags. The /doc, /sandbox and /testcases pages should normally be in the subject namespace, except in the namespaces that do not have the MediaWiki [[w:m:Help:Link#Subpage feature|subpage feature]] enabled: Main, File, Mediawiki and Category. (But currently we only show the /sandbox and /testcases links from User, User talk, Template and Template talk namespaces.) There are also a whole bunch of other technical reasons why the /doc page must be stored under the talk page for those (but only those) namespaces. This template automatically points its [create] links for the /doc, /sandbox and /testcases to the right namespace. ===Technical details=== The preload page for the /doc [create] link is [[Template:Documentation/preload]]. The preload pages for the /sandbox and /testcases [create] links are [[Template:Documentation/preload-sandbox]] and [[Template:Documentation/preload-testcases]]. The preload page for the /sandbox [mirror] link is [[Template:Documentation/mirror]]. For more details, see the [[Template talk:Documentation|talk page]]. ====Full syntax==== 
{{Documentation}}

{{Documentation
 | content =
}}

{{Documentation
| [path to documentation page]
| heading-style = 
| heading = 
| link box = 
}}
===See also=== * {{tl|Documentation subpage}}, a notice placed at the top of a /doc subpage explaining its role and including a link to the page it documents. * {{tl|Barnstar documentation}}, a variant of {{tl|Documentation}} for use with [[w:Wikipedia:Barnstars|barnstar]] templates. * {{tl|Documentation/color scheme}} presents the color scheme used by {{tl|Documentation}}. * [[w:Wikipedia:Template documentation]] is a how-to guide to template documentation. * [[w:Wikipedia:Template sandbox and test cases]] explains the use of /sandbox and /testcases subpages and includes more information about template testing. [[Category:Template documentation pages| ]]

revision.comment: Created page with "--[[ -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- -- -- -- NAMESPACE DETECT -- -- -- -- This module implements the {{namespace detect}} template in Lua, with a -- -- few improvements: all namespaces and all namespace aliases are..."
revision.text: --[[ -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- -- -- -- NAMESPACE DETECT -- -- -- -- This module implements the {{namespace detect}} template in Lua, with a -- -- few improvements: all namespaces and all namespace aliases are supported, -- -- and namespace names are detected automatically for the local wiki. The -- -- module can also use the corresponding subject namespace value if it is -- -- used on a talk page. Parameter names can be configured for different wikis -- -- by altering the values in the "cfg" table in -- -- Module:Namespace detect/config. -- -- -- -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- --]] local data = mw.loadData('Module:Namespace detect/data') local argKeys = data.argKeys local cfg = data.cfg local mappings = data.mappings local yesno = require('Module:Yesno') local mArguments -- Lazily initialise Module:Arguments local mTableTools -- Lazily initilalise Module:TableTools local ustringLower = mw.ustring.lower local p = {} local function fetchValue(t1, t2) -- Fetches a value from the table t1 for the first key in array t2 where -- a non-nil value of t1 exists. for i, key in ipairs(t2) do local value = t1[key] if value ~= nil then return value end end return nil end local function equalsArrayValue(t, value) -- Returns true if value equals a value in the array t. Otherwise -- returns false. for i, arrayValue in ipairs(t) do if value == arrayValue then return true end end return false end function p.getPageObject(page) -- Get the page object, passing the function through pcall in case of -- errors, e.g. being over the expensive function count limit. if page then local success, pageObject = pcall(mw.title.new, page) if success then return pageObject else return nil end else return mw.title.getCurrentTitle() end end -- Provided for backward compatibility with other modules function p.getParamMappings() return mappings end local function getNamespace(args) -- This function gets the namespace name from the page object. local page = fetchValue(args, argKeys.demopage) if page == '' then page = nil end local demospace = fetchValue(args, argKeys.demospace) if demospace == '' then demospace = nil end local subjectns = fetchValue(args, argKeys.subjectns) local ret if demospace then -- Handle "demospace = main" properly. if equalsArrayValue(argKeys.main, ustringLower(demospace)) then ret = mw.site.namespaces[0].name else ret = demospace end else local pageObject = p.getPageObject(page) if pageObject then if pageObject.isTalkPage then -- Get the subject namespace if the option is set, -- otherwise use "talk". if yesno(subjectns) then ret = mw.site.namespaces[pageObject.namespace].subject.name else ret = 'talk' end else ret = pageObject.nsText end else return nil -- return nil if the page object doesn't exist. end end ret = ret:gsub('_', ' ') return ustringLower(ret) end function p._main(args) -- Check the parameters stored in the mappings table for any matches. local namespace = getNamespace(args) or 'other' -- "other" avoids nil table keys local params = mappings[namespace] or {} local ret = fetchValue(args, params) --[[ -- If there were no matches, return parameters for other namespaces. -- This happens if there was no text specified for the namespace that -- was detected or if the demospace parameter is not a valid -- namespace. Note that the parameter for the detected namespace must be -- completely absent for this to happen, not merely blank. --]] if ret == nil then ret = fetchValue(args, argKeys.other) end return ret end function p.main(frame) mArguments = require('Module:Arguments') local args = mArguments.getArgs(frame, {removeBlanks = false}) local ret = p._main(args) return ret or '' end function p.table(frame) --[[ -- Create a wikitable of all subject namespace parameters, for -- documentation purposes. The talk parameter is optional, in case it -- needs to be excluded in the documentation. --]] -- Load modules and initialise variables. mTableTools = require('Module:TableTools') local namespaces = mw.site.namespaces local cfg = data.cfg local useTalk = type(frame) == 'table' and type(frame.args) == 'table' and yesno(frame.args.talk) -- Whether to use the talk parameter. -- Get the header names. local function checkValue(value, default) if type(value) == 'string' then return value else return default end end local nsHeader = checkValue(cfg.wikitableNamespaceHeader, 'Namespace') local aliasesHeader = checkValue(cfg.wikitableAliasesHeader, 'Aliases') -- Put the namespaces in order. local mappingsOrdered = {} for nsname, params in pairs(mappings) do if useTalk or nsname ~= 'talk' then local nsid = namespaces[nsname].id -- Add 1, as the array must start with 1; nsid 0 would be lost otherwise. nsid = nsid + 1 mappingsOrdered[nsid] = params end end mappingsOrdered = mTableTools.compressSparseArray(mappingsOrdered) -- Build the table. local ret = '{| class="wikitable"' .. '\n|-' .. '\n! ' .. nsHeader .. '\n! ' .. aliasesHeader for i, params in ipairs(mappingsOrdered) do for j, param in ipairs(params) do if j == 1 then ret = ret .. '\n|-' .. '\n| ' .. param .. '' .. '\n| ' elseif j == 2 then ret = ret .. '' .. param .. '' else ret = ret .. ', ' .. param .. '' end end end ret = ret .. '\n|-' .. '\n|}' return ret end return p

{{Used in system}} {{Module rating|protected}} {{Lua|Module:Namespace detect/data|Module:Yesno|Module:Arguments|Module:TableTools}} This module allows you to output different text depending on the [[WP:NAMESPACE|namespace]] that a given page is in. It is a [[WP:Lua|Lua]] implementation of the {{tl|namespace detect}} template, with a few improvements: all namespaces and all namespace aliases are supported, and namespace names are detected automatically for the local wiki. == Usage == 
{{#invoke: Namespace detect | main
| page              = 
| main              = 
| talk              = 


| portal            = 
| category          = 
| user 	            = 
| wikipedia         = 
| mediawiki         = 
| book              = 
| timedtext         = 
| template          = 
| special           = 
| media             = 
| file              = 
| image             = 
| help 	            = 
| module            = 

| other             = 
| demospace         = 

| subjectns         = 
}}
== Parameters == * '''main''' - text to return if the page is in the main namespace. * '''talk''' - text to return if the page is in a talk namespace. This can be any talk namespace - it will match any of "Talk:", "Wikipedia talk:", "User talk:", etc. * Subject namespace parameters, e.g. '''wikipedia''', '''user''', '''file'''... - the text to return if the page is in the corresponding namespace. This module accepts all subject namespaces as parameters, including [[Wikipedia:Namespace#Aliases|namespace aliases]] and [[Wikipedia:Namespace#Virtual namespaces|virtual namespaces]]. See below for a list of supported values. * '''other''' - text to return if no parameters for the page's namespace were specified. This text is also returned if {{para|demospace}} is set to an invalid namespace value. * '''subjectns''' - if on a talk page, use the corresponding subject page. Can be set with values of "yes", "y", "true" or "1". * '''demopage''' - specifies a page to detect the namespace of. If not specified, and if the {{para|demospace}} parameter is not set, then the module uses the current page. * '''demospace''' - force the module to behave as if the page was in the specified namespace. Often used for demonstrations. === Namespace parameters === Possible values for subject namespace parameters are as follows: {{#invoke:Namespace detect|table}} == Table function == Use the following to display a table with the different possible namespace parameters: {{#invoke:Namespace detect|table|talk=''yes''}} To include the parameter for talk namespaces, use {{para|talk|yes}}. == Porting to different wikis == This module is designed to be portable. To use it on a different wiki, all you need to do is to change the values in [[Module:Namespace detect/config]]. Instructions are available on that page. == Technical details == The module uses a data page at [[Module:Namespace detect/data]]. This page is loaded with [[mw:Extension:Scribunto/Lua reference manual#mw.loadData|mw.loadData]], which means it is processed once per page rather than once per #invoke. This was done for performance reasons.

revision.text:
== Introduction == Dracolist Malonia, a significant entity in its region, holds a storied past marked by resilience, ideological transformation, and evolving political landscapes. Situated amid influential neighbors and dynamic economies, Malonia has shaped, and been shaped by, a complex tapestry of alliances, conflicts, and philosophical movements. At its heart, Dracolist Malonia is recognized for its deep-rooted cultural identity, the rise of [[Dracoism]]—a unifying yet polarizing ideology—and a historical progression of governmental reforms that have transformed its political and social structure over centuries. Geographically, Dracolist Malonia is strategically located, surrounded by notable powers and critical trade routes that have played a substantial role in its economic development. The nation’s borders encompass varied landscapes, from rugged mountains to fertile valleys, which have allowed for a diverse economy historically focused on agriculture, mining, and later, industrial production. This varied topography also provides natural defensive advantages, which have often been crucial in its military strategies and defense postures. In modern times, the influence of Dracoism has shaped Malonia's political and social fabric, fostering a unique blend of ideological and pragmatic governance that seeks both cultural preservation and national resilience. This ideology, which rose to prominence in the late 20th century, continues to shape policy decisions and the overall identity of Malonia within the global community. With its history divided into distinct periods of reform, conflict, and ideological resurgence, each era of Malonia’s past contributes to an understanding of its current status. The following sections examine the major historical epochs of Dracolist Malonia, tracing its evolution across political, economic, and military spheres. == History of Dracolist Malonia == ===== Early Period (pre-1731) ===== The early history of Malonia is characterized by a mosaic of small states, tribal confederations, and proto-kingdoms that laid the groundwork for its later unification. The people of early Malonia organized themselves into distinct clans and regional powers, often competing for territory and resources. This era saw the formation of the early cultural and social norms that would later evolve into national ideologies and influence the emergence of Dracoism. == Three Government Changes and Peace Period (1731 - 1905) == This period marked a transformative era for Malonia as it navigated through three distinct forms of government, each bringing the country under increasing influence and control by the [[Vesperan Empire]]. From a monarchy to a republic, and later a constitutional democracy, Malonia’s political evolution was deeply shaped by Vesperan interference. By the early 1900s, Malonia had effectively become a puppet state, controlled economically, politically, and militarily by the Vesperan Empire. This dependence on Vesperan oversight would persist until the early 20th century, setting the stage for Malonia's role in the Great War and its eventual liberation. ==== Monarchy (1731 - 1785) ==== The period began under a monarchy, with kings exercising centralized control over Malonia's territories. At this stage, Malonia still retained a degree of independence, though Vesperan influence began to seep into the court and government. The Vesperans, through diplomatic ties and economic leverage, slowly gained sway over Malonia’s decision-making, setting up a foundation for their future control. ==== Republican Era (1785 - 1850) ==== Following a revolution, Malonia transitioned to a republic, ostensibly shifting power away from the monarchy and toward a council-based government. However, the Vesperan Empire saw an opportunity to expand its influence, providing "support" to Malonia’s fledgling republic in the form of economic aid, military advisors, and strategic partnerships. This intervention allowed the Vesperans to install loyalists within the Malonian government, ensuring policies favorable to their interests. By the mid-1800s, Malonia's republican government was heavily reliant on Vesperan backing, with most significant political decisions approved, if not outright dictated, by Vesperan representatives. This reliance on Vesperan support compromised Malonia’s sovereignty, transforming the republic into a nominally independent state under the de facto control of the Vesperan Empire. ==== Constitutional Democracy (1850 - 1905) ==== In response to demands for greater representation, Malonia transitioned to a constitutional democracy. This new government promised increased political freedoms and citizen participation; however, it was little more than a façade. The Vesperan Empire, having solidified its hold on Malonia, used this "democratic" period to further entrench its control. By strategically placing loyalists in positions of power and limiting Malonia’s autonomy through political and economic dependencies, the Vesperans ensured that Malonia functioned primarily as a Vesperan satellite state. Throughout this period, Malonia's legislative and executive branches were largely subservient to Vesperan interests. Key policies, particularly in trade and military alliances, were directed by the Vesperan Empire, and any attempt at asserting independence was quickly quashed. By the 1910s, Malonia had effectively lost all political autonomy, operating entirely under Vesperan oversight. This period of total puppeting stifled Malonian self-determination, causing resentment among the populace and fostering the seeds of future resistance. ===== Economic Sphere ===== Under Vesperan influence, Malonia’s economy became geared toward supporting the Vesperan Empire’s needs. While the monarchy and early republic maintained some economic independence, the constitutional period saw Vesperan control reach unprecedented levels. Vesperan officials controlled Malonia’s major industries, dictated trade policies, and imposed tariffs that favored Vesperan goods. Key resources, particularly raw materials like metals and agricultural products, were directed almost exclusively to Vesperan markets, stunting the development of a self-sustaining economy. In addition, Vesperan-backed banks and corporations dominated Malonia’s financial landscape, profiting from Malonian resources and labor. The economic exploitation contributed to growing poverty and hardship among the Malonian people, leading to widespread dissatisfaction with both the puppet government and its Vesperan overlords. ===== Military Sphere ===== Malonia’s military underwent substantial changes under Vesperan oversight. During the monarchy, Malonia maintained a modest force, primarily focused on internal stability and defense. However, as the Vesperan influence grew, Malonia’s military was increasingly repurposed to serve Vesperan interests. Under the constitutional democracy, Malonia’s army and navy were largely subordinated to Vesperan command. Vesperan officers held influential advisory positions, dictating Malonia’s military strategies and operations. This control extended to troop deployments, with Malonian soldiers often deployed to serve in Vesperan conflicts or to protect Vesperan economic interests abroad. By the early 20th century, Malonia’s military had been effectively co-opted, its primary purpose reduced to supporting the Vesperan Empire’s expansionist ambitions. == The [[Avant Great War|Great War]] and the [[United Alignment]] Nations' Intervention (1949) == The conclusion of the Great War marked a turning point for Malonia, which had suffered greatly under Vesperan exploitation. With the defeat of the Vesperan Empire and the subsequent intervention by the United Alignment Nations (UAN), Malonia was finally liberated from foreign domination. The UAN, a coalition of anti-imperialist nations and former colonies, sought to dismantle puppet states established by empires like the Vesperan and to promote self-determination for oppressed regions. This intervention fundamentally altered Malonia’s trajectory, paving the way for a new era of independence, albeit one marked by significant challenges. === Dissolution of Puppet Government: ===
Upon victory in 1949, the UAN moved swiftly to dismantle the Vesperan-installed puppet regime. The Malonian government was restructured with a provisional administration overseen by UAN representatives and local leaders committed to independence. This transitional period saw a focus on re-establishing Malonia’s sovereignty and creating a new political system based on democratic principles.
Formation of an Independent State: In the early 1950s, Malonia adopted a constitution designed to prevent the return of foreign control. The new government aimed to rebuild public trust, introducing measures to safeguard against undue influence from outside powers. The period of UAN oversight saw the establishment of Malonia’s first truly independent government, with national elections and the restoration of civil liberties.
=== Economic Sphere === '''Economic Reconstruction and Nationalization:''' The UAN’s influence extended to economic policy, encouraging Malonia to reclaim its industries and reduce dependence on foreign capital. Major industries that had been controlled by Vesperan corporations were nationalized, and the government implemented land reforms to redistribute resources and promote economic equity. This program of economic recovery aimed to create a self-reliant economy, though the effects of Vesperan exploitation left Malonia with limited resources and substantial financial challenges. '''Foreign Aid and Economic Alliances:''' Recognizing Malonia’s economic vulnerability, the UAN provided financial assistance and facilitated trade agreements with other newly independent nations. These economic alliances helped Malonia rebuild its infrastructure, though dependence on foreign aid also brought new challenges. As the country struggled to stabilize its economy, debates emerged regarding the balance between self-reliance and international cooperation. === Military Sphere === '''Military Restructuring and Independence:''' With the Vesperan military advisors removed, Malonia’s military underwent a significant restructuring. The UAN assisted in establishing an independent defense force, trained to prioritize national defense over foreign intervention. This restructured military was smaller but more efficient, with a focus on internal security and territorial integrity rather than serving as an auxiliary force for foreign powers. '''Defense Policies and Regional Alliances:''' As a newly independent state, Malonia initially maintained a defensive posture, wary of threats from neighboring nations with whom it had once been entangled in conflict under Vesperan command. To strengthen its sovereignty, Malonia entered into defense agreements with UAN member states, ensuring collective security while maintaining an emphasis on autonomy. This approach marked a departure from its former role as a vassal of the Vesperan Empire, establishing Malonia as a self-governing entity capable of defending its interests. == Legacy of UAN Intervention == The intervention by the United Alignment Nations fundamentally reshaped Malonia’s identity and governance. The post-war liberation fueled a sense of national pride and laid the foundation for ideological movements that would emerge in the following decades. While the transition to independence was fraught with economic hardship and political uncertainty, it also represented the dawn of a new era of self-determination. The experience of subjugation under the Vesperan Empire created a strong desire for autonomy and resilience, values that would later be championed by the Dracoist movement in Malonia. == Dracoism Rising (1993 - 2001) == The rise of Dracoism in Malonia from 1993 to 2001 marked a period of ideological consolidation, political centralization, and nationalistic fervor. Rooted in the ideals of self-sufficiency, cultural unity, and state-led development, Dracoism emerged as a powerful force in Malonia following decades of foreign exploitation, war, and social upheaval. The Dracoist movement tapped into the collective desire for national pride, resilience, and independence from external influences. By championing the principles of Dracoism, Malonian leaders sought to redefine the nation's identity, reassert its sovereignty, and create a more unified society. Dracoism advocated for a strong centralized government, an economy geared towards national interests, and a disciplined military force capable of defending Malonia from any potential threats. These principles resonated deeply with the Malonian populace, particularly in the context of their history of subjugation under the Vesperan Empire. Over the course of this period, Dracoism transformed Malonia’s political, economic, and military structures, leaving an indelible mark on the nation’s development. === Political Sphere === The rise of Dracoism brought about a shift towards authoritarian governance, as the movement's leaders believed that a strong, centralized state was essential for maintaining unity and advancing national goals. This new political structure prioritized the Dracoist principles of unity, loyalty, and strength, aiming to forge a tightly controlled state free from foreign interference. ===== '''Establishment of a Dracoist Government:''' ===== In 1993, the Dracoist Party gained significant influence within the government, and soon after, Dracoist leaders assumed key positions in the administration. The political system was restructured to concentrate power in the hands of the Dracoist leadership, and the state was reoriented to align with Dracoist ideals. Elections, while maintained in a nominal sense, were largely symbolic, as opposition parties faced increasing restrictions and censorship. ===== Propaganda and State Ideology: ===== To cultivate public support, the Dracoist government employed an extensive propaganda apparatus, emphasizing Malonia's unique cultural identity, historical resilience, and Dracoism's role in restoring national pride. The state-controlled media portrayed Dracoist leaders as protectors of the nation, frequently referencing Malonia’s past struggles and the sacrifices made by previous generations. This narrative fostered a strong sense of patriotism and loyalty among citizens, reinforcing the Dracoist regime's authority. ===== Suppression of Opposition: ===== Dracoism’s authoritarian approach led to the suppression of dissenting voices and political opposition. Critics of the regime were often labeled as “anti-national” or “foreign sympathizers,” and were subject to censorship, surveillance, and, in some cases, imprisonment. Dracoist leaders viewed dissent as a threat to national unity, and the political climate became increasingly restrictive. Civil liberties were curtailed in the name of preserving stability, and citizens were encouraged to report any signs of anti-Dracoist sentiment to authorities. === Economic Sphere === Dracoism placed a strong emphasis on economic self-sufficiency, aiming to reduce Malonia's dependence on foreign imports and influence. This economic policy, often described as “Dracoist Economics,” prioritized state control over key industries, protectionism, and national productivity. ===== State-Controlled Industries: ===== Under Dracoist rule, Malonia’s economy was reorganized to align with the state’s strategic priorities. Key industries, including energy, mining, steel production, and agriculture, were nationalized or brought under stringent government oversight. This allowed the Dracoist government to control resource allocation and prioritize industries that were deemed essential to national security and development. ===== Protectionist Policies and Trade Restrictions: ===== Dracoism's economic doctrine advocated for protectionism as a means of shielding Malonia’s economy from external influences. Tariffs on foreign goods were increased, and imports were restricted to prevent competition with domestic industries. By limiting foreign trade, the Dracoist government aimed to foster a self-reliant economy, with Malonia producing most of its own goods and relying minimally on external sources. ===== Agricultural and Industrial Programs: ===== Recognizing the importance of food security and industrial independence, the Dracoist regime launched large-scale programs to increase agricultural output and industrial productivity. Farmers were incentivized to produce staple crops, and urban workers were mobilized to support factory production. This emphasis on national productivity was often accompanied by Dracoist slogans and propaganda, encouraging citizens to “work for the strength of Malonia.” While these policies did increase output in certain sectors, they often came at the expense of individual freedoms and were enforced with strict compliance measures. ===== Economic Challenges and Autarky: ===== Although Dracoist policies aimed to foster a resilient economy, the emphasis on self-sufficiency created certain economic challenges. With limited access to foreign technology and innovation, Malonia’s industries struggled to modernize, resulting in inefficiencies and lower-quality goods. However, the Dracoist leadership viewed these sacrifices as necessary for achieving economic independence, and any criticism of the system was swiftly suppressed. === Military Sphere === The Dracoist movement instilled a renewed emphasis on military strength, viewing a powerful and disciplined military as essential to safeguarding Malonia’s sovereignty and Dracoist values. This period saw a dramatic transformation of Malonia’s armed forces, with increased funding, new strategic doctrines, and a focus on cultivating a fiercely loyal and ideologically committed military. ===== '''Fortress Malonia Doctrine''': ===== Dracoist ideology placed a strong emphasis on defense, creating a “fortress” around Malonia’s borders to ensure that the nation could withstand any foreign threat. Malonian territory was heavily fortified, with strategic defense installations, reinforced borders, and rapid-response units designed to counter incursions. This defensive posture was complemented by an equally strong commitment to expansion, with military forces trained and equipped for both border protection and offensive operations. ===== '''Expansion-Oriented Military Strategy''': ===== In line with Dracoism’s belief in Malonia’s destiny to dominate, the military was reoriented to facilitate territorial expansion. The army adopted a proactive stance, with units specifically trained for rapid deployment, territorial control, and infrastructure management in newly acquired areas. Military academies emphasized tactics not only for defense but for conquest, preparing officers and soldiers to execute Malonia’s expansionist objectives effectively. ===== Political Indoctrination within the Military: ===== The Dracoist regime placed a strong emphasis on ideological commitment within the ranks, ensuring that soldiers were loyal not only to the nation but also to Dracoism itself. Training programs included political education, where recruits learned about Malonia’s history, Dracoist principles, and the importance of national unity. Soldiers were taught that they were part of a greater mission to protect Malonian values and sovereignty, making the military a highly cohesive and ideologically aligned institution. ===== Militarization of Society: ===== Dracoism’s influence extended beyond the armed forces and into civilian life, as the regime promoted a culture of preparedness and resilience. Citizens were encouraged to take part in military training programs and civil defense exercises, fostering a sense of collective responsibility for national security. The Dracoist government also established youth organizations focused on physical fitness, discipline, and loyalty to the state, preparing future generations to support Malonia’s defense.

revision.text:
{{Infobox country | conventional_long_name = Templar of Saxonia | native_name = {{lang|fr|Templar vun Saxonien}} | common_name = Saxonia | image_flag = [[File:Saxonia Flag|thumb]] | alt_flag = White flag divided by a blood-red line with a circle under a portcullis in its middle. | national_motto =
{{native phrase |fr|"Über den Wolken"|italics=off}}
"Above the Clouds" | national_anthem =
[[March of the Heavenly Knights]]
[[Marsch der Himmleschen Ridder]] | official_languages = {{hlist |[[Saxonian language|Saxonian]] |[[Theorin language|Theorin]]}} | demonym = Saxonian | capital = [[Saxonia]] | government_type = [[Theocratic Elective Monarchy]] | leader_title1 = [[Prince-Templar]] | leader_name1 = [[Godesfurct Waels]] | leader_title2 = [[Minister]] | leader_name2 = [[Iain Duncan]] | legislature = [[Orderly Chamber]] | population_census = 7,023,832 | population_census_year = 2009 | established_event1 = Unification | established_date1 = 981 | established_event2 = Current Constitution | established_date2 = 1947 | currency = [[Saxonian Taler]] | currency_code = TAL | calling_code = +211 | cctld = .sa }} The Templar of Saxonia is a sovereign nation located to the north of the Theorin Commonwealth, to the east of Mons, and to the west of Pestera. According to the 2009 census, it has a population of 47,091,834 and is thus one of the more densely populated countries in the region. The history of Saxonia as an independent state dates back to 981: through the Edict of Palatzina, the castles controlled by the Order of the Saxonian Temple were reorganised into the Sovereign Order of Saxonia with a territory spanning parts of the North Coast and moving about 100 km inland towards Theorin. The Sovereign Order was extinguished under pressure from the Spring Parliament of 1451, giving way to the Templar of Saxonia as an entity separate from the order and allowing civilians and laymen alike to join the halls of government. A period of economic and demographic expansion ensued, leading to further colonisation inland and border friction with the Theorin. (...) ''awaiting Theorin lore confirmation'' With the election of prior Ulfer Nidderbuerg as Prince-Templar in 1946, the power struggle was ended and the reformists appeared to have won. A group of legal scholars was thus invited to the capital to elaborate a constitution, which was finished and adopted in 1947. During the country's first elections in that same year, the social liberal Constitutional Movement won a majority and instituted a series of social and economic reforms. A two-party system developed under its successor parties starting from 1958. Rotating governments formed by the Liberal Movement and the Castle Party lasted until 1972, when a coup led by general Kärel Schuze overthrew democracy and suspended the constitution to establish an anti-socialist, authoritarian dictatorship. Schuze reigned as Prince-Templar until his death in 1991, which was followed by a process of gradual democratisation that is still ongoing as of 2009. === Before the Sovereign Order === To understand the history of Saxonia, one must first understand the history of the Order of the Saxonian Temple. Legend says it was founded over 2000 years ago by Saint Saxen, who became its first Templar. The earliest archeological findings of Saxonian religious sites date back to around the year 200 in the southern coast of Theorin, the birthplace of Uniadorationism. The Order seemed to have appeared shortly after the establishment of the first uniadorationist monasteries, leading experts to believe it may have been a bellicose offshoot of monastic movements as a result of religious and political unrest around the 4th century. The Order gradually expanded its influence, but remained a marginal force. A few religious sites are attested in central Theorin by the year 600. Its true period of expansion only happened decades later, when deforestation efforts linked to an expanding agricultural sector lead many peasants to go north into the Mouwe forest. The Order followed its movements, as several chronicles from the time attest. It offered protection from bandits and pagan tribes to the peasants and established its own fiefdom in the region, becoming a major regional player both politically and religiously. Its position was strengthened in particular by a network of castles built as "border fortifications" as the deforestation efforts advanced.

revision.text: The Orinian Empire, a Regional Power within the continent of [[Khalari]], who's status as a regional power is defined by great leadership and legacy. The Empire was established in 1680 by ''Ádám Bako'', the first Emperor of the [[Orinian Empire]]. Overtime the Empire would establish strong ties with other countries like the [[Union of Zhensanov]] and some of its neighbors. However, it is weary of the [[Ba'athist Republic of Volgastan]] due to the two competing as status for regional power on the continent. Additionally, the Orinian Empire has grown distrustful of the [[AGGPI]] due to recent actions and how they have handled them.

revision.text:
The Orinian Empire, a Regional Power within the continent of [[Khalari]], who's status as a regional power is defined by great leadership and legacy. The Empire was established in 1680 by ''Ádám Bako'', the first Emperor of the [[Orinian Empire]]. Overtime the Empire would establish strong ties with other countries like the [[Union of Zhensanov]] and some of its neighbors. However, it is weary of the [[Ba'athist Republic of Volgastan]] due to the two competing as status for regional power on the continent. as well as the [[Svetkhanul Republic]] to its east. Additionally, the Orinian Empire has grown distrustful of the [[AGGPI]] due to recent actions and how they have handled them.
'''The Beginning of the Orinian Empire'''
The [[Orinian Empire]] was at first a group of nations that were related in culture and identity, but never had a sense of unity. They all lived in relative peace, only facing threats from neighboring nations who didn’t like them. However, one man would change the course of these nations by calling for Unity. This man, who was known as Ádám Bako, would have a dream of a Greater Nation and a Golden Age. This Golden Age came to him as a vision where envisioned cities of great importance with the people of the nation cheering on the leaders of the nation in giving them an Era of Prosperity. With this call of Unity, the nations would unify into the Orinian Empire during the 17th Century. During this time, the Orinian Empire would begin to seek a vision of itself, starting out as a nation of towns and villages, that would slowly progress into defining itself as a regional power within the region. However, not all was sound within the the Khalari Continent, where they were. A nation within its northern regions known as [[Vorkutangrad]], did not like the newly founded Orinian Empire due to a tense conflict in the cultural and ethnic scene. Due to this, it would start a relationship between the Cultures of the Orinian Empire, often called the Magyars as well as the Suomalaiset. This would be known as the Magyar-Suomalaiset Accords, a long standing agreement that made the two groups of people friends, which serves as foundation for the alliance. A nation home to the Suomalaiset is the [[Kolklennan Empire]], which overtime, would form a friendly relationship with the nation. Ádám Bako would unfortunately die at the Age of 90 from Natural Causes, but his absence of power wouldn’t be left unfilled. His eldest daughter, Erzsébet Bako, would take the reign of her father. She would usher in the Age of Dreams for the Orinian Empire.
'''The Age of Dreams'''
The Age of Dreams would be welcomed as Empress Erzsébet would take her fathers reign and bring in this age. The Age of Dreams would span from the death of Ádám Bako in 1650 and continue over the next two centuries. Erzsébet was someone who knew what her father wanted for the people, so it was no surprise that the people, in return, would show support for her actions. She helped in establishing neutral relations with most of the neighboring nations outside of the [[Svetkhanul Republic]], a nation with a large border to the Empire’s East. The two nations were never on the best of terms, both being at odds with each other since the two nations founding. The relationship between Orinian and Svetkhanul is one that fluctuates overtime. Outside of foreign affairs, she made great strides domestically. She would establish the first designated road networks within the nation as well as help establish the economy of the Orinian Empire, adopting foreign currency. Erzsébet’s reign would unfortunately come to an end when she would die peacefully in her sleep at the age of 85. The next in the Bako Dynasty to take the reins of the Empire would be her brother Elek Bako, someone who would establish the history of the Orinian Military. He would kickstart the [[1st Orinian-Svetkhanul War]] in 1740, with the war ending in a draw between the two powers. He would also begin to modernize the Orinian Military into using modern rifles and artillery for the time. Elek established a precedent of military growth that would continue through the future monarchs. Elek would die at the age of 80 due to heart failure. Next would begin the Age of Modernization.
'''Age of Modernization'''
The Age of Modernization would carry through the remainder of the years, starting with the reign of Sandor Bako, the father of István Bako. During the reign of Emperor Elek, there would be a trend of the Bako Dynasty ruining the lives of the rural population due to it being slightly increasingly hard to live in those regions. While Elek denied these allegations in office, Sandor would own up to them, giving the Rural Population the promise that their life would be better. His reign was most remembered for the [[2nd Orinian-Svetkhanul War]] in 1900 as well as his reforms making the [[Orinian Empire]] into what it is. The War would end in another draw, as an armistice was signed in order to keep peace between the two nations for as long as possible. Additionally he would also begin the distrust the [[AGGPI]] seeing their recent actions on the other side of the world and seeing their mismanagement of conflicts around the world. The reforms that were passed would set the Empire up into modernizing to become more industrial, eventually becoming a powerhouse in the Civilian Market. Emperor Sandor would also establish a long standing trade agreement with the [[Union of Zhensanov]], a nation who was quite powerful. The two would establish a long standing trade deal that would benefit the [[Orinian Empire]] greatly. In 1985, his father would pass, temporarily passing the leadership to his brother Adrienn Bako for 10 years before the current Emperor, István Bako, would take the position as Emperor. During those 10 years, it would start the relationship with the [[Ba’athist Republic of Volgastan]], who is seen as an weary enemy due to their expansionist policies. Due to those the two would be at odds with each other and never see eye to eye. However, this wouldn’t stop Emperor István Bako in leading his people into a better age into the 21st Century.

revision.text:
'''1. Territorial Boundaries'''
''Clause 1.1: Recognition of Sovereign Borders''
All signatory nations recognize and respect the sovereign borders as established by the Istragarde Commission during the [[Treaty Accord of 1951]]. These borders are considered legally binding and immutable unless modified through mutual agreement ratified by a two-thirds majority of signatory states.
''Clause 1.2: Border Violations''
Encroachments beyond recognized borders will be considered acts of hostility unless sanctioned by the [[Istragarde Tribunal]] or justified by exceptional circumstances, including humanitarian crises or population migrations officially declared by the treaty’s oversight body.
''Clause 1.3: Maritime Boundaries''
[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exclusive_economic_zone Exclusive Economic Zones] (EEZ) extend four hundred nautical miles from recognized coastlines, with territorial waters reaching up to fifteen nautical miles. Disputes over contested maritime regions must be resolved through the Tribunal’s arbitration process. ----'''2. Enforcement Mechanisms'''
''Clause 2.1: Oversight Authority''
The Istragarde Treaty establishes the '''Istragarde Tribunal''', a symbolic international legal body meant to mediate disputes related to the treaty’s terms. However, the Tribunal lacks direct enforcement powers, relying solely on the voluntary compliance of signatory nations.
''Clause 2.2: Compliance Audits''
Annual compliance audits are recommended but not mandated. Nations are encouraged to submit reports detailing their adherence to the treaty’s terms. Failure to comply results in sanctions, including expulsion from treaty councils or formal condemnations.
''Clause 2.3: International Response''
In cases of extreme violations, such as unauthorized invasions, the treaty allows for a “Joint Action Request” to be issued. This request seeks coalition support from willing signatories, though participation is voluntary. ----'''3. Diplomatic Arbitration'''
''Clause 3.1: Dispute Resolution Framework''
Disputes arising from territorial, maritime, or jurisdictional conflicts must be submitted to the Istragarde Tribunal. Deliberations are to be held within sixty days of a formal complaint being lodged, unless delayed by procedural disputes.
''Clause 3.2: Tribunal Composition''
The Tribunal consists of appointed representatives from five rotating signatory states, selected every six years. Appointees are to act with neutrality,<ref>Historical precedent shows this clause is rarely enforced.</ref>
''Clause 3.3: Appeals Process''
Rulings by the Tribunal are considered final. However, nations may submit an appeal for reconsideration if new evidence emerges within one year of the original ruling.<ref>This process has often been dismissed as a formality due to the Tribunal’s limited authority.</ref> ----'''4. Prohibited Actions and Limitations'''
''Clause 4.1: Acts of Aggression''
No signatory shall engage in open warfare without formal declaration and sufficient cause, as determined by the Tribunal.<ref>In practice, this clause has been widely ignored due to the Tribunal's inability to impose penalties.</ref>
''Clause 4.2: Restricted Weapons''
In recognition of the devastating potential of certain weapons on human populations and the environment, signatories agree to:
# Strongly discourage the use of chemical, biological, or nuclear weapons in any conflict involving signatory states. # Promote dialogue and negotiation to ensure mutual restraint in the development, stockpiling, and deployment of such weapons. # Encourage transparency among signatories regarding the possession and intended use of restricted weaponry through voluntary disclosures submitted to the Istragarde Tribunal.<ref>Though the treaty failed to ban chemical, biological, or nuclear weapons outright, it "strongly discourages" their use in conflicts involving signatories, recommending “mutual restraint.” This ambiguity has led to frequent circumventions.</ref>
''Clause 4.3: War Crimes Accountability''
To uphold the principles of humanitarian standards, the signatories hereby agree:
# To avoid conduct deemed to cause unnecessary harm to civilian populations during times of armed conflict. # To provide captured combatants with basic rights and protections, as defined by customary international practices. # To encourage the establishment of independent inquiries in cases of alleged humanitarian violations, the findings of which shall be submitted to the Istragarde Tribunal for review.<ref>The treaty vaguely references “humanitarian standards” without defining specific war crimes or associated punishments. Signatories are “encouraged” to abide by these standards, leaving much open to interpretation.</ref>
== Historical Consequences and Legacy == The Istragarde Treaty, signed in 1951, was a reluctant attempt at stabilizing a fractured world after the [[Avant Great War|Great War]] and the Continuation War. Its creation marked a desperate collective effort to impose order amid widespread devastation. Despite its strict clauses, the treaty’s enforcement mechanisms were purposefully weak, leaving nations bound by law yet liberated by practicality.
==== The [[Invasion of Bátravalka]] (1971) ==== The most infamous early example of the treaty’s limitations came in nineteen seventy-one, when the [[Karlist Perzam]] invoked the Istragarde treaty’s territorial clauses to justify its surprise invasion of the mineral-rich highlands of [[Bátravalka]]. Citing “historical claims” and the need to “protect ethnic [[Perzamic]] communities,” Perzam's leaders framed their expansionist campaign as a legal reclamation of lost lands. International condemnation followed, though no military response was organized due to the treaty’s non-binding enforcement protocols.
==== [[Volgastan’s Expansionist Doctrine]] (1980s-1990s) ==== Inspired by Perzam’s precedent, the [[Volgastan Baathist Republic|Baathist Republic of Volgastan]] launched a series of aggressive territorial expansions throughout the nineteen eighties and nineties. Citing similar justifications grounded in the treaty's clauses on “territorial integrity” and “cultural protection,” Volgastan redrew borders through calculated military campaigns. The Istragarde Tribunal issued repeated rulings against Volgastan, but no united action followed. By the mid-nineties, Volgastan controlled vast territories far beyond its original borders, cementing the treaty's reputation as a diplomatic shield for opportunistic expansion.
=== EEZ Conflicts in the Straits of Avangard === The territorial disputes between the People's Republic of Mariposa and its northern neighbors, [[Imperial Rhovland|Rhovland]] and [[Legion of Astoria|Astoria]], have long centered on the strategic control of two critical straits—natural chokepoints for trade, resource extraction, and military positioning. Both conflicts are rooted in the overlapping Exclusive Economic Zones (EEZs) defined under the Istragarde Treaty, which grants nations up to four hundred nautical miles of resource rights but leaves enforcement to the nations themselves.
==== The Mariposa-Rovlin Conflict: The Eastern Strait ==== The waters between the People's Republic of Mariposa and the Imperial Rhovland-controlled territories in the east are particularly tense. This narrow strait serves as a critical artery for Rhovland’s naval and commercial fleets, while Mariposa views it as an essential zone for economic exploitation. Both nations claim overlapping EEZs, leading to frequent skirmishes involving fishing vessels, oil prospecting ships, and patrol boats.
In 1983, tensions flared when Mariposa deployed a fleet of survey ships escorted by naval corvettes to explore potential underwater oil reserves within the contested zone. Rhovland responded by dispatching destroyers, leading to a weeks-long naval standoff. Despite the Istragarde Tribunal ruling in favor of shared exploitation rights, neither side has abided by the decision, with Mariposa regularly accusing Rhovland of "economic sabotage" while Rhovland condemns Mariposa for "reckless maritime adventurism."
==== The Mariposa-Astoria Conflict: The Western Strait ==== The western strait, flanked by Mariposa and Astoria, is similarly fraught. Unlike the Eastern Strait, this waterway is vital for Astoria’s shipping lanes and national security. Mariposa, however, has claimed the area as part of its historical fishing grounds and sought to expand its maritime rights. This provocative move has sparked outrage in Astoria, which argues this move violates the Istragarde Treaty’s clause on territorial extensions.
The conflict escalated in 1990 when Mariposa seized an Astorian fishing trawler, accusing it of poaching within its waters. Astoria retaliated by imposing an economic blockade on Mariposan shipping through the strait, crippling Mariposa’s export-dependent economy for months. Diplomatic talks mediated by third-party nations resulted in temporary trade agreements.
==== Impact on Regional Stability ==== The unresolved EEZ disputes have turned these straits into volatile flashpoints, destabilizing the surrounding region and undermining the Istragarde Treaty’s intended purpose of reducing territorial conflicts. The lack of enforceable mechanisms has emboldened both Mariposa and its rivals to escalate their claims in past and present, risking larger-scale conflict. Despite periodic calls for arbitration, the Istragarde Tribunal’s rulings are often ignored, leaving the disputes to fester as symbols of Avant-Garde's fractured international order.

== '''Istragarde Treaty''' == The '''Istragarde Treaty''', formally known as the '''International Agreement for the Regulation of Territorial and Maritime Boundaries and Conduct in Conflict''', was signed on '''July 14, 1951''', in the city of [[Istragarde]]. This treaty marked the culmination of years of negotiation following the devastation of the [[Avant Great War|'''Avant''' '''Great War (1937–1949)''']] and the '''Continuation War (1949–1951)''', which had left the world fractured, war-torn, and desperate for a semblance of stability.
The treaty was forged as a reluctant compromise among the world’s most powerful and war-weary nations. Though starkly divided by ideological, economic, and territorial ambitions, these nations recognized the urgent need to establish a basic framework of international norms to prevent the recurrence of global warfare. Negotiations were held in Istragarde, a city located in [[Socialist Republic of Aurendale]].
The Istragarde Treaty’s provisions were ambitious in scope but limited in enforcement. They sought to delineate territorial and maritime boundaries, encourage restraint in the use of devastating weaponry, and outline humanitarian standards for warfare. While the treaty succeeded in establishing clear guidelines on paper, its weak enforcement mechanisms and vague definitions left much open to interpretation, allowing conflicts to persist and new ones to arise under its shadow.
'''1. Territorial Boundaries'''
''Clause 1.1: Recognition of Sovereign Borders''
All signatory nations recognize and respect the sovereign borders as established by the Istragarde Commission during the [[Treaty Accord of 1951]]. These borders are considered legally binding and immutable unless modified through mutual agreement ratified by a two-thirds majority of signatory states.
''Clause 1.2: Border Violations''
Encroachments beyond recognized borders will be considered acts of hostility unless sanctioned by the [[Istragarde Tribunal]] or justified by exceptional circumstances, including humanitarian crises or population migrations officially declared by the treaty’s oversight body.
''Clause 1.3: Maritime Boundaries''
[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exclusive_economic_zone Exclusive Economic Zones] (EEZ) extend four hundred nautical miles from recognized coastlines, with territorial waters reaching up to fifteen nautical miles. Disputes over contested maritime regions must be resolved through the Tribunal’s arbitration process. ----'''2. Enforcement Mechanisms'''
''Clause 2.1: Oversight Authority''
The Istragarde Treaty establishes the '''Istragarde Tribunal''', a symbolic international legal body meant to mediate disputes related to the treaty’s terms. However, the Tribunal lacks direct enforcement powers, relying solely on the voluntary compliance of signatory nations.
''Clause 2.2: Compliance Audits''
Annual compliance audits are recommended but not mandated. Nations are encouraged to submit reports detailing their adherence to the treaty’s terms. Failure to comply results in sanctions, including expulsion from treaty councils or formal condemnations.
''Clause 2.3: International Response''
In cases of extreme violations, such as unauthorized invasions, the treaty allows for a “Joint Action Request” to be issued. This request seeks coalition support from willing signatories, though participation is voluntary. ----'''3. Diplomatic Arbitration'''
''Clause 3.1: Dispute Resolution Framework''
Disputes arising from territorial, maritime, or jurisdictional conflicts must be submitted to the Istragarde Tribunal. Deliberations are to be held within sixty days of a formal complaint being lodged, unless delayed by procedural disputes.
''Clause 3.2: Tribunal Composition''
The Tribunal consists of appointed representatives from five rotating signatory states, selected every six years. Appointees are to act with neutrality,<ref>Historical precedent shows this clause is rarely enforced.</ref>
''Clause 3.3: Appeals Process''
Rulings by the Tribunal are considered final. However, nations may submit an appeal for reconsideration if new evidence emerges within one year of the original ruling.<ref>This process has often been dismissed as a formality due to the Tribunal’s limited authority.</ref> ----'''4. Prohibited Actions and Limitations'''
''Clause 4.1: Acts of Aggression''
No signatory shall engage in open warfare without formal declaration and sufficient cause, as determined by the Tribunal.<ref>In practice, this clause has been widely ignored due to the Tribunal's inability to impose penalties.</ref>
''Clause 4.2: Restricted Weapons''
In recognition of the devastating potential of certain weapons on human populations and the environment, signatories agree to:
# Strongly discourage the use of chemical, biological, or nuclear weapons in any conflict involving signatory states. # Promote dialogue and negotiation to ensure mutual restraint in the development, stockpiling, and deployment of such weapons. # Encourage transparency among signatories regarding the possession and intended use of restricted weaponry through voluntary disclosures submitted to the Istragarde Tribunal.<ref>Though the treaty failed to ban chemical, biological, or nuclear weapons outright, it "strongly discourages" their use in conflicts involving signatories, recommending “mutual restraint.” This ambiguity has led to frequent circumventions.</ref>
''Clause 4.3: War Crimes Accountability''
To uphold the principles of humanitarian standards, the signatories hereby agree:
# To avoid conduct deemed to cause unnecessary harm to civilian populations during times of armed conflict. # To provide captured combatants with basic rights and protections, as defined by customary international practices. # To encourage the establishment of independent inquiries in cases of alleged humanitarian violations, the findings of which shall be submitted to the Istragarde Tribunal for review.<ref>The treaty vaguely references “humanitarian standards” without defining specific war crimes or associated punishments. Signatories are “encouraged” to abide by these standards, leaving much open to interpretation.</ref>
== Historical Consequences and Legacy == The Istragarde Treaty, signed in 1951, was a reluctant attempt at stabilizing a fractured world after the [[Avant Great War|Great War]] and the Continuation War. Its creation marked a desperate collective effort to impose order amid widespread devastation. Despite its strict clauses, the treaty’s enforcement mechanisms were purposefully weak, leaving nations bound by law yet liberated by practicality.
==== The [[Invasion of Bátravalka]] (1971) ==== The most infamous early example of the treaty’s limitations came in nineteen seventy-one, when the [[Karlist Perzam]] invoked the Istragarde treaty’s territorial clauses to justify its surprise invasion of the mineral-rich highlands of [[Bátravalka]]. Citing “historical claims” and the need to “protect ethnic [[Perzamic]] communities,” Perzam's leaders framed their expansionist campaign as a legal reclamation of lost lands. International condemnation followed, though no military response was organized due to the treaty’s non-binding enforcement protocols.
==== [[Volgastan’s Expansionist Doctrine]] (1980s-1990s) ==== Inspired by Perzam’s precedent, the [[Volgastan Baathist Republic|Baathist Republic of Volgastan]] launched a series of aggressive territorial expansions throughout the nineteen eighties and nineties. Citing similar justifications grounded in the treaty's clauses on “territorial integrity” and “cultural protection,” Volgastan redrew borders through calculated military campaigns. The Istragarde Tribunal issued repeated rulings against Volgastan, but no united action followed. By the mid-nineties, Volgastan controlled vast territories far beyond its original borders, cementing the treaty's reputation as a diplomatic shield for opportunistic expansion.
=== EEZ Conflicts in the Straits of Avangard === The territorial disputes between the People's Republic of Mariposa and its northern neighbors, [[Imperial Rhovland|Rhovland]] and [[Legion of Astoria|Astoria]], have long centered on the strategic control of two critical straits—natural chokepoints for trade, resource extraction, and military positioning. Both conflicts are rooted in the overlapping Exclusive Economic Zones (EEZs) defined under the Istragarde Treaty, which grants nations up to four hundred nautical miles of resource rights but leaves enforcement to the nations themselves.
==== The Mariposa-Rovlin Conflict: The Eastern Strait ==== The waters between the People's Republic of Mariposa and the Imperial Rhovland-controlled territories in the east are particularly tense. This narrow strait serves as a critical artery for Rhovland’s naval and commercial fleets, while Mariposa views it as an essential zone for economic exploitation. Both nations claim overlapping EEZs, leading to frequent skirmishes involving fishing vessels, oil prospecting ships, and patrol boats.
In 1983, tensions flared when Mariposa deployed a fleet of survey ships escorted by naval corvettes to explore potential underwater oil reserves within the contested zone. Rhovland responded by dispatching destroyers, leading to a weeks-long naval standoff. Despite the Istragarde Tribunal ruling in favor of shared exploitation rights, neither side has abided by the decision, with Mariposa regularly accusing Rhovland of "economic sabotage" while Rhovland condemns Mariposa for "reckless maritime adventurism."
==== The Mariposa-Astoria Conflict: The Western Strait ==== The western strait, flanked by Mariposa and Astoria, is similarly fraught. Unlike the Eastern Strait, this waterway is vital for Astoria’s shipping lanes and national security. Mariposa, however, has claimed the area as part of its historical fishing grounds and sought to expand its maritime rights. This provocative move has sparked outrage in Astoria, which argues this move violates the Istragarde Treaty’s clause on territorial extensions.
The conflict escalated in 1990 when Mariposa seized an Astorian fishing trawler, accusing it of poaching within its waters. Astoria retaliated by imposing an economic blockade on Mariposan shipping through the strait, crippling Mariposa’s export-dependent economy for months. Diplomatic talks mediated by third-party nations resulted in temporary trade agreements.
==== Impact on Regional Stability ==== The unresolved EEZ disputes have turned these straits into volatile flashpoints, destabilizing the surrounding region and undermining the Istragarde Treaty’s intended purpose of reducing territorial conflicts. The lack of enforceable mechanisms has emboldened both Mariposa and its rivals to escalate their claims in past and present, risking larger-scale conflict. Despite periodic calls for arbitration, the Istragarde Tribunal’s rulings are often ignored, leaving the disputes to fester as symbols of Avant-Garde's fractured international order.

# Strongly discourage the use of chemical, biological, or nuclear weapons in any conflict involving signatory states. # Promote dialogue and negotiation to ensure mutual restraint in the development, stockpiling, and deployment of such weapons. # Encourage transparency among signatories regarding the possession and intended use of restricted weaponry through voluntary disclosures submitted to the Istragarde Tribunal.<ref>Though the treaty failed to ban chemical, biological, or nuclear weapons outright, it "strongly discourages" their use in conflicts involving signatories, recommending “mutual restraint.” This ambiguity has led to frequent circumventions.</ref>
''Clause 4.3: War Crimes Accountability''
To uphold the principles of humanitarian standards, the signatories hereby agree:
# To avoid conduct deemed to cause unnecessary harm to civilian populations during times of armed conflict. # To provide captured combatants with basic rights and protections, as defined by customary international practices. # To encourage the establishment of independent inquiries in cases of alleged humanitarian violations, the findings of which shall be submitted to the Istragarde Tribunal for review.<ref>The treaty vaguely references “humanitarian standards” without defining specific war crimes or associated punishments. Signatories are “encouraged” to abide by these standards, leaving much open to interpretation.</ref>
== Historical Consequences and Legacy == ==== The [[Invasion of Bátravalka]] (1971) ==== The most infamous early example of the treaty’s limitations came in nineteen seventy-one, when the [[Karlist Perzam]] invoked the Istragarde treaty’s territorial clauses to justify its surprise invasion of the mineral-rich highlands of [[Bátravalka]]. Citing “historical claims” and the need to “protect ethnic [[Perzamic]] communities,” Perzam's leaders framed their expansionist campaign as a legal reclamation of lost lands. International condemnation followed, though no military response was organized due to the treaty’s non-binding enforcement protocols.
==== [[Volgastan’s Expansionist Doctrine]] (1980s-1990s) ==== Inspired by Perzam’s precedent, the [[Volgastan Baathist Republic|Baathist Republic of Volgastan]] launched a series of aggressive territorial expansions throughout the nineteen eighties and nineties. Citing similar justifications grounded in the treaty's clauses on “territorial integrity” and “cultural protection,” Volgastan redrew borders through calculated military campaigns. The Istragarde Tribunal issued repeated rulings against Volgastan, but no united action followed. By the mid-nineties, Volgastan controlled vast territories far beyond its original borders, cementing the treaty's reputation as a diplomatic shield for opportunistic expansion.
=== EEZ Conflicts in the Straits of Avangard === The territorial disputes between the [[People's Republic of Mariposa]] and its northern neighbors, [[Imperial Rhovland|Rhovland]] and [[Legion of Astoria|Astoria]], have long centered on the strategic control of two critical straits—natural chokepoints for trade, resource extraction, and military positioning. Both conflicts are rooted in the overlapping Exclusive Economic Zones (EEZs) defined under the Istragarde Treaty, which grants nations up to four hundred nautical miles of resource rights but leaves enforcement to the nations themselves.
==== The Mariposa-Rovlin Conflict: The Eastern Strait ==== The waters between the People's Republic of Mariposa and the Imperial Rhovland-controlled territories in the east are particularly tense. This narrow strait serves as a critical artery for Rhovland’s naval and commercial fleets, while Mariposa views it as an essential zone for economic exploitation. Both nations claim overlapping EEZs, leading to frequent skirmishes involving fishing vessels, oil prospecting ships, and patrol boats.
In 1983, tensions flared when Mariposa deployed a fleet of survey ships escorted by naval corvettes to explore potential underwater oil reserves within the contested zone. Rhovland responded by dispatching destroyers, leading to a weeks-long naval standoff. Despite the Istragarde Tribunal ruling in favor of shared exploitation rights, neither side has abided by the decision, with Mariposa regularly accusing Rhovland of "economic sabotage" while Rhovland condemns Mariposa for "reckless maritime adventurism."
==== The Mariposa-Astoria Conflict: The Western Strait ==== The western strait, flanked by Mariposa and Astoria, is similarly fraught. Unlike the Eastern Strait, this waterway is vital for Astoria’s shipping lanes and national security. Mariposa, however, has claimed the area as part of its historical fishing grounds and sought to expand its maritime rights. This provocative move has sparked outrage in Astoria, which argues this move violates the Istragarde Treaty’s clause on territorial extensions.
The conflict escalated in 1990 when Mariposa seized an Astorian fishing trawler, accusing it of poaching within its waters. Astoria retaliated by imposing an economic blockade on Mariposan shipping through the strait, crippling Mariposa’s export-dependent economy for months. Diplomatic talks mediated by third-party nations resulted in temporary trade agreements.
==== Impact on Regional Stability ==== The unresolved EEZ disputes have turned these straits into volatile flashpoints, destabilizing the surrounding region and undermining the Istragarde Treaty’s intended purpose of reducing territorial conflicts. The lack of enforceable mechanisms has emboldened both Mariposa and its rivals to escalate their claims in past and present, risking larger-scale conflict. Despite periodic calls for arbitration, the Istragarde Tribunal’s rulings are often ignored, leaving the disputes to fester as symbols of Avant-Garde's fractured international order.

Kaonism

Kaonism is a moderate collectivist ideology rooted in ethical statecraft, social equilibrium, and moral economic planning. Considered the direct philosophical predecessor to modern Taoism, Kaonism was first formulated in the mid-19th century in the Kingdom of Saochi. It combined communal economic theory, ritual governance, and proto-spiritual thought into a distinct ideological system. Though it never gained mass support within Saochi, it would later spread eastward, where its principles quietly shaped the development of Taoist doctrine, particularly in the People's Federation of Xanaqu.

Unlike revolutionary socialism or liberal collectivism, Kaonism stressed the need for rhythm between society's parts—what its founder, Liao Zhengyuan (廖正元), called "the binding harmony between man, work, and rule." The ideology's core premise was not the overthrow of hierarchy, but its ethical transformation and synchronization with the people's needs and spiritual condition.

Origins

Kaonism emerged during the Saochian Reorganization Period (circa 1841–1863), a time marked by famine, fractured governance, urban discontent, and the collapse of agrarian traditions. Amid these tensions, Liao Zhengyuan, a low-ranking scholar and civil administrator, began publishing a series of treatises that proposed a new political worldview—one that rejected the decay of aristocracy, the cruelty of industrial absolutism, and the chaos of populist revolt. He envisioned instead a "kaonic order": a form of governance that would maintain balance by cultivating spiritual clarity, collective labor, and restrained leadership.

His most famous works, The Bond of People (1844) and Measure of the Self-State (1848), proposed a framework for collective ownership of essential resources, rotating civic leadership based on moral fitness, and the use of ritual and seasonal cycles to regulate social life. These texts circulated among reformist literati and provincial cooperatives, but were banned following the Purge of 1865, when the central court violently cracked down on alternative philosophies. Liao was arrested and disappeared soon after, presumed to have died in exile.

Ideological Foundations

Balanced Collectivism

Kaonism advocates for the collective management of core industries and land, but rejects violent redistribution and total egalitarianism. Ownership is to be stewarded, not atomized. The goal is synthesis, not sameness—where farmers, artisans, and officials all contribute to a shared economic body while maintaining their social identities.

The Syntonic State

The state is seen as a spiritual conductor, meant to synchronize the rhythms of society rather than dominate them. Governance must follow the Fourfold Alignment—mind, work, nature, and law—which ensures decisions are taken in accordance with seasonal cycles, ethical codes, and communal benefit.

Moralized Authority

Leaders in a kaonic society are selected not solely for ability, but for demonstrated moral balance and spiritual clarity. Bureaucrats undergo training not only in policy but in meditation, literature, and ethical jurisprudence. Power must always be aligned with restraint.

Ritual over Revolution

Unlike revolutionary ideologies, Kaonism rejects the violent overthrow of systems, believing such disruption harms social equilibrium. Change must come through ritualized reform, reflection, and the cultivation of civic institutions that reinforce moral behavior.

Anti-Exploitative, Not Anti-State

Kaonists do not oppose hierarchy on principle, but rather oppose exploitation. The state is to be transformed, not dismantled—made into a reflective body, not an instrument of force. The real enemy is not structure, but dissonance within it.

Legacy and Evolution

Though Kaonism failed to gain mass support in its birthplace of Saochi, its ideas took root in exile. After Liao Zhengyuan's disappearance, surviving adherents—many of them guild leaders, scholars, and rural cooperativists—migrated eastward across the continent. In particular, Kaonist cells found refuge in the fractured borderlands of Xanaqu, where industrialization and land reform debates created fertile ground for philosophical experimentation.

There, Kaonism slowly evolved, merging with folk cosmology, labor organizing networks, and emerging political schools. By the early 20th century, Xing Tao, a former Kaonist-influenced student, synthesized these currents into a modern ideology: Taoism. Xing would later refer to Liao Zhengyuan as "the one who saw the Path before it had a name."

Core Kaonist concepts—such as the Fourfold Alignment, moralized governance, and non-revolutionary collectivism—became central to Taoist governance theory. Elements of Kaonist ritualism survive in state practices, including seasonal policy councils, leader meditation rites, and the civic concept of harmonic tenure.

Cultural Remnants

Though largely erased from Saochian official history, Kaonism remains studied in select academic institutions across Xanaqu and appears in the Historical Appendix of the Taoist Manifesto. In some rural communities, Kaonist-inspired rites—such as the Harvest Reconciliation Ceremony and Rotational Oath-Giving—are still practiced during major festivals.

A bronze statue of Liao Zhengyuan stands in Taojin Academy, flanked by the phrase he once wrote in exile:

"Order is not a chain but a rhythm. When all things move in time, there is no need for force."
